footballers.story: Mario Gomez was the archetype of the six-yard predator, a striker who lived for the split-second inside the box and left the build-up to others. Born in Baden-Wurttemberg to a Spanish father and a German mother, he announced himself by firing Stuttgart to a shock Bundesliga title in 2007. A club-record move took him to Bayern Munich, where his goals piled up by the season and a European treble followed. Later chapters in Florence, Istanbul and Wolfsburg proved his poacher's instinct travelled anywhere. Never the most fashionable name, he simply kept scoring, and few of his generation did it more ruthlessly.
didYouKnow: A serious knee injury ruled him out of contention for Germany's squad at the 2014 World Cup, the tournament they went on to win.
His father, Jose, is Spanish, hailing from a village near Granada, while his mother is German.
He scored his own penalty in Bayern's 2012 Champions League final shootout, but they still lost on their own ground to Chelsea.

footballers.name: Harry Kewell
clues: My career was defined by serious injuries as much as by my talent.
I was voted the greatest footballer my country has ever produced.
I was a surprise pick to start a Champions League final, only to limp off inside the first half-hour as my team began a famous comeback.
I came through a famous English academy, won the FA Youth Cup, and broke into a side that reached a European semi-final in 2001.
I became the first Australian to win the Champions League.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 22nd of September 1978. I played 58 times for my country, scoring 17 goals.
footballers.story: Out of Smithfield in Sydney came a left foot that could open any door. At Leeds United he was pure electricity, a teenager tearing down the flank with defenders trailing, the jewel of a young side that gatecrashed Europe. Injuries would nag at his Liverpool years, yet he was there in Istanbul in 2005, the first Australian to lift the European Cup. For the Socceroos he was the golden boy, among the youngest ever to pull on the shirt and later a driving force behind their return to the World Cup after 32 years away. Wizard of Oz, they called him, and the name fit.
didYouKnow: He was the first Australian to win the UEFA Champions League, with Liverpool in 2005.
In 2012 he was voted Australia's greatest ever soccer player by fans, players and the media.
He won the PFA Young Player of the Year award in 2000 during his Leeds United days.

footballers.name: Leighton Baines
clues: I was a lethal penalty taker, scoring my first ten in the Premier League without a miss.
In the 2012-13 season I created more chances than any player in Europe's top five leagues, despite not playing for one of the Premier League's big six.
For years I was kept out of my national side by another left-back.
My left-sided understanding with Steven Pienaar became one of the league's most feared partnerships.
I am the left-back remembered as an Everton great of the modern era.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 11th of December 1984. I played 30 times for my country, scoring 1 goal.
footballers.story: For thirteen seasons the number three shirt at Goodison belonged to one man. Leighton Baines arrived from Wigan in 2007 and quietly became the finest attacking full-back in the country, a left foot capable of whipping in free-kicks and gliding penalties into the corner. He rarely sought the spotlight, an introvert happier in a record shop than a press room, yet his overlapping runs down the Everton left were poetry in blue. England never quite found room for him, and a major trophy never came. Even so, few players have been loved by one club so completely.
didYouKnow: A master from the spot, he converted his first ten Premier League penalties without missing.
For years he was kept out of the England side by first-choice left-back Ashley Cole.
A devoted indie-music fan, he became close friends with musician Miles Kane.

footballers.name: Louis Saha
clues: My first big move came after I lit up the second tier and helped win promotion to the top flight.
I lifted the Champions League trophy in 2008.
I played mostly in England, for Fulham, Manchester United and Everton.
I earned a reputation as a gifted striker whose talent was matched only by his bad luck with fitness.
I was a French international forward who won Premier League titles and that 2008 European crown at Manchester United.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 8th of August 1978. I played 20 times for my country, scoring 4 goals.
footballers.story: Louis Saha was the striker football never quite let you keep. Fast, powerful and blessed with a lovely first touch, he tore up the First Division at Fulham and earned a January move to Manchester United, where he scored freely whenever his body allowed. That was the cruelty of his career, a gifted forward forever wrestling with injuries that stole whole seasons and softened his prime. Even so he collected the biggest medals in the game and left a signature moment at Everton, a low bullet past Petr Cech in an FA Cup final. When fit, he was as good as any centre-forward in England.
didYouKnow: In the 2009 FA Cup final for Everton he scored after around 25 seconds, at the time the fastest goal in the history of the competition's final.
His career was repeatedly disrupted by injuries that cost him long spells and blunted his prime years.
He first broke through at Fulham, firing them to promotion and earning his big move to Manchester United.

footballers.name: John Obi Mikel
clues: I began my career as a creative attacking midfielder before being reinvented in a much deeper, defensive role.
I won the Africa Cup of Nations in 2013 with my national side.
I won the Premier League title in 2010.
As a teenager, two of England's biggest clubs both announced they had signed me, sparking a famous transfer tug-of-war.
In 2012 I became a European champion at club level.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 22nd of April 1987. I played 89 times for my country, scoring 6 goals.
footballers.story: Before he ever kicked a ball in the Premier League, John Obi Mikel was the boy two giants fought over, with Chelsea and Manchester United both claiming his signature in one of the strangest transfer sagas English football has known. Chelsea won the tug-of-war, and for more than a decade he rewarded them, quietly recast from a dribbling No. 10 into the unshowy heartbeat in front of the back four. He shielded, screened and started attacks while others took the applause, playing the full 120 minutes of the 2012 Champions League final in Munich. Later came China, Middlesbrough and Stoke, a long unwinding of a serious career. For Nigeria he was captain and talisman, and rarely has a player done so much while asking for so little credit.
didYouKnow: As a teenager he became the centre of a famous transfer saga when both Chelsea and Manchester United announced they had signed him.
He began his career as an attacking midfielder before being reinvented as a disciplined holding midfielder at Chelsea.
He captained Nigeria to the 2013 Africa Cup of Nations title and to a bronze medal at the 2016 Olympic Games.

footballers.name: Jermaine Pennant
clues: I once played La Liga football in Spain for Real Zaragoza.
I was, at the time, the record signing for a trainee when Arsenal paid £2 million for me at age 15.
I started a Champions League final against AC Milan.
Pundits often bracketed me with fast, tricky wingers like Aaron Lennon and Theo Walcott.
I started the 2011 FA Cup final but ended up on the losing side with Stoke City.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 15th of January 1983. I was never capped by my country at senior level.
footballers.story: He arrived at Arsenal as a fifteen-year-old prodigy, a record fee for a trainee and a weight of expectation few boys could shoulder. The gift was never in doubt: a right foot full of tricks, blistering pace, a low centre of gravity that left full-backs grabbing at shadows. He never quite mastered it all, drifting through a dozen clubs, but on his best nights he was simply unplayable. Liverpool saw that version often, and in Athens in 2007 he was arguably the finest man on the pitch as Milan edged the final. England, strangely, never came calling. The talent, though, was always the story.
didYouKnow: Arsenal signed him from Notts County at just 15 for around 2 million pounds, a record fee for a trainee at the time.
He scored a hat-trick on his first Premier League start for Arsenal, in a 6-1 win over Southampton in May 2003.
He started the 2007 Champions League final for Liverpool against AC Milan, one of the few Englishmen to appear in a European Cup final.

footballers.name: Boudewijn Zenden
clues: I was born in the city that gave its name to a landmark European treaty signed in 1992.
I scored in the final as Middlesbrough lifted the 2004 League Cup, their first major trophy.
Yesterday's player and I were team-mates at the same club, and we both played in the 2007 Champions League final we lost to AC Milan.
A Dutch winger, I spent two seasons at Liverpool and earlier played for both Barcelona and Chelsea.
Throughout my career people knew me by the nickname "Bolo".
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 15th of August 1976. I played 54 times for my country, scoring 7 goals.
footballers.story: They called him Bolo, and for a decade Boudewijn Zenden was Dutch football's great wanderer, a quick, two-footed winger who could operate down either flank or tuck inside. He broke through at PSV, then chased the light at Barcelona, winning La Liga in his first season at the Camp Nou. England became his long home: a big-money move to Chelsea, then a reinvention at Middlesbrough, where he scored in the club's first major final and became a fans' favourite. Liverpool followed, and with it a night in Athens and a European Cup final. Rarely the headline act, Zenden was the sort of clever, willing footballer every great side quietly needs.
footballers.numbers: 7 goals in 54 caps for the Netherlands
didYouKnow: He was born in Maastricht, the Dutch city that gave its name to the 1992 European treaty.
He scored in Middlesbrough's 2004 League Cup final win over Bolton, the club's first major trophy in its history.
He played in the 2007 Champions League final for Liverpool, who lost to AC Milan in Athens.

footballers.name: Mario Balotelli
clues: I won a treble as a teenager under Jose Mourinho before moving to England.
I was the first black player to represent my country at a major tournament.
I provided the assist for one of the most dramatic title-winning goals in Premier League history, the only Premier League assist of my career.
Born in Sicily to Ghanaian parents, I was raised by a foster family in the north of Italy.
My nickname was 'Super Mario'.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 12th of August 1990. I played 36 times for my country, scoring 14 goals.
footballers.story: Few forwards blurred genius and chaos quite like Mario Balotelli. A teenage prodigy in Jose Mourinho's treble-winning Inter, he crossed to Manchester City as English football's most bewildering talent, capable of a sublime finish one minute and a needless red card the next. He powered City to their first league title in a generation, then lit up Euro 2012 with two thunderbolts past Germany. AC Milan, Liverpool and Nice all chased the same maddening promise. Unplayable on his day and unpredictable on every other, Super Mario never once stopped surprising.
didYouKnow: After scoring twice in Manchester City's 6-1 win at Old Trafford, he lifted his jersey to reveal a shirt reading 'Why Always Me?'.
His pass for Sergio Aguero's dramatic title-winning goal against QPR in 2012 was the only Premier League assist of his entire career.
At Euro 2012 he became the first black player to represent Italy at a major tournament, then scored both goals in the semi-final win over Germany.

footballers.name: David James
clues: Off the pitch I was known for my physique, my tattoos and my modelling work.
I made 572 Premier League appearances, among the most in the competition's history.
In 2008 I won the FA Cup with Portsmouth.
For years I held the record for the most Premier League clean sheets, before Petr Cech overtook me.
My frequent mistakes as a goalkeeper for Liverpool earned me the nickname "Calamity James".
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 1st of August 1970. I played 53 times for my country, without scoring.
footballers.story: For all the headlines that branded him Calamity James, David James was a giant who outlasted almost everyone. He rose at Liverpool, lifting the League Cup in 1995, then carried his 6ft 4in frame through Aston Villa, West Ham and Manchester City before finding real peace on the south coast. At Portsmouth he finally won the FA Cup in 2008, the crowning day of a Premier League career that stretched to 572 games, more than any goalkeeper had played before him. And at 39, when younger men had long retired, he stood as England's number one at the 2010 World Cup. Errors made his nickname, but longevity made his legend.
didYouKnow: The tabloids nicknamed him "Calamity James" for a run of high-profile errors, a tag he never quite shook despite a long and decorated career.
He made 572 Premier League appearances, for years the most by any goalkeeper in the competition's history.
At 39 he was England's number one at the 2010 World Cup, and his bow against Algeria made him the oldest debutant in the tournament's history.

footballers.name: Gylfi Sigurdsson
clues: I am regarded as one of the finest free-kick takers of my generation.
Everton made me their club-record signing for a fee of around 45 million pounds.
At Euro 2016, my nation beat England on the way to the quarter-finals.
I played for Swansea twice and was their star man.
I was the creative talisman of Iceland's golden generation, a free-kick specialist who starred for Swansea and Everton.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 8th of September 1989. I played 86 times for my country, scoring 28 goals.
footballers.story: Gylfi Sigurdsson was the creative heartbeat of Iceland's golden generation, a left foot that could pick a lock or bend a set piece into the top corner from thirty yards. He announced himself on loan at Swansea, earned a big move to Hoffenheim and then Tottenham, and returned to south Wales to become the Premier League's most reliable dead-ball threat. In 2017 Everton made him their club-record signing at around 40 million pounds, betting on the vision and free-kicks that lit up Goodison. But it was in blue and white that he mattered most, the talisman who drove tiny Iceland to the Euro 2016 quarter-finals and became his nation's all-time leading scorer.
didYouKnow: He is Iceland's all-time leading goalscorer, with 28 goals in 86 international appearances.
He was one of the Premier League's finest free-kick specialists, a genuine threat from any dead ball around the box.
As Iceland's creative talisman he inspired the run to the Euro 2016 quarter-finals, the tournament where his side famously beat England.

footballers.name: Kevin Davies
clues: I have committed more fouls than any other player in Premier League history.
I won my only international cap at the age of 33, one of the oldest debutants in half a century.
My bustling, physical style made me a proper old-fashioned target man.
A big-money transfer once took me to a top-flight club for around 7.5 million pounds.
I spent a decade at Bolton Wanderers, becoming their captain under a famously no-nonsense manager.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 26th of March 1977. I played once for my country, without scoring.
footballers.story: Some strikers glide; Kevin Davies waded in with elbows out and shirt untucked, the last of the true English target men. He announced himself as a teenager in Chesterfield's fairytale 1997 FA Cup run, then bounced between Southampton and Blackburn before finding his true home at Bolton. Under Sam Allardyce he became the fulcrum of everything, chesting balls down, winning fouls, bullying centre-backs into a decade of grim submission. He led the line and eventually the team, a captain forged in the Reebok's cold and clatter. England came calling absurdly late, but by then his legend was already carved in bruises.
honours: Football League Third Division play-off promotion (Chesterfield, 1995)
Football League One play-off promotion (Preston North End, 2015)
didYouKnow: He holds the record for the most fouls committed in Premier League history, racking up over 1,000 across his career.
He won his solitary England cap absurdly late, aged 33, coming off the bench against Montenegro in 2010 as the country's oldest debutant since 1950.
As a teenager he starred in Chesterfield's romantic 1997 FA Cup run to the semi-finals, scoring a hat-trick against Bolton along the way.

footballers.name: Gerard Deulofeu
clues: I hold the record for the most appearances ever made for my country's under-21 team.
I scored twice in an FA Cup semi-final to send Watford to the 2019 final.
I came through Barcelona's famed La Masia youth academy.
I was a tricky, direct winger who became a fan favourite at Everton.
In Italy I had a loan spell at AC Milan.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 13th of March 1994. I played 4 times for my country, scoring 1 goal.
footballers.story: Gerard Deulofeu emerged from Barcelona's La Masia carrying the weight of enormous expectation, a dazzling dribbler who seemed destined for the Camp Nou first team but never quite made it his own. Instead his career became a restless tour of Europe, taking in two spells at Everton, loans at Sevilla and AC Milan, and eventually a home of sorts at Udinese in Italy. His finest English day came for Watford, when he twisted defenders inside out and dragged the club to Wembley. For all the clubs and the miles, the abiding memory is of a player whose feet could do things few others dared try.
didYouKnow: One of the most heralded talents to come through Barcelona's La Masia academy, he was tipped for stardom but never established himself in the first team.
He holds the record for the most appearances ever made for Spain's under-21 side, and remains their all-time leading scorer at that level.
He scored twice off the bench in the 2019 FA Cup semi-final, turning a two-goal deficit around to send Watford past Wolves and into the final.

footballers.name: Jonjo Shelvey
clues: In 2016-17 I helped my club win the EFL Championship title.
I was signed by Rafael Benitez and later played under Kenny Dalglish, without ever quite making my mark.
I became Charlton Athletic's youngest-ever player, making my senior debut at just 16.
I am a central midfielder famed for an immaculate range of passing.
As a teenager I earned a big-money move to Liverpool, then spent seven years as the playmaker at Newcastle United.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 27th of February 1992. I played 6 times for my country, without scoring.
footballers.story: Jonjo Shelvey announced himself absurdly young, a sixteen-year-old at home in Charlton's midfield before most boys his age had left school. Liverpool came calling for the teenager, drawn to a right foot that could thread a pass sixty yards without breaking stride. He never quite settled at Anfield, but at Swansea and then Newcastle he found his stage, dictating games with the range and swagger of a proper playmaker. On Tyneside he became the heartbeat, the man to unlock a stubborn defence with one raking diagonal, and he helped haul the club back to the top flight as Championship winners. England called six times, a nod to a talent never in doubt.
didYouKnow: He became Charlton Athletic's youngest ever player when he debuted at 16 years and 59 days old in April 2008.
Liverpool signed him as a teenager, tempted by a passing range that could pick out team-mates from sixty yards.
He spent seven years as Newcastle United's midfield playmaker, dictating their tempo from deep between 2016 and 2023.

footballers.name: Jurgen Klinsmann
clues: I both played and managed my country at a World Cup.
In my one full season in England I was voted Footballer of the Year.
I won UEFA Cups in both Italy and Germany.
Away from the pitch I became a qualified helicopter pilot and settled in California.
On my debut for an English club I mocked my own reputation with a theatrical diving celebration.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 30th of July 1964. I played 108 times for my country, scoring 47 goals.
footballers.story: The son of a Stuttgart baker who once shaped Swabian pretzels before he shaped defences, Jurgen Klinsmann was a striker of restless energy and ruthless finishing. He plundered goals across Europe with Stuttgart, Inter, Monaco and Bayern, then conquered a doubting England in a single glorious season at Tottenham, disarming his critics with a self-mocking swan-dive on his debut. For Germany he was a serial winner, lifting the World Cup in 1990 and captaining the Euro 96 champions. Later he returned as a coach, firing a young Germany to the semi-finals on home soil in 2006.
didYouKnow: Before turning professional he completed an apprenticeship as a baker, a trade rooted in his family's business near Stuttgart.
On his Tottenham debut in 1994 he scored and then launched into a self-mocking swan-dive celebration, poking fun at his reputation for going to ground easily.
As a coach he led Germany to third place at the 2006 home World Cup and later managed the United States and South Korea.

footballers.name: Joe Hart
clues: Four times I won my league's award for the best in my position.
I have been on loan to West Ham and Torino.
I won a domestic treble at Celtic later in my career.
I won a number of Premier Leagues, playing in goal.
But I left that club when a new manager arrived and quickly decided I was not part of his plans.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 19th of April 1987. I played 75 times for my country, without scoring.
footballers.story: Joe Hart was England's great glovesman of a golden generation, a shot-stopper whose roar and reflexes made the number one shirt his own for the best part of a decade. Plucked from Shrewsbury, he became the heartbeat of Manchester City's rise, winning two league titles and a fistful of Golden Gloves as the club climbed from also-rans to champions. Then Pep Guardiola arrived, wanted a keeper comfortable with the ball at his feet, and Hart was cast out, drifting through Torino, West Ham and Burnley. Rather than fade, he answered in Scotland, winning a domestic treble at Celtic and closing the curtain with a Scottish Cup on his final afternoon. Few keepers have fallen so far and risen so well.
didYouKnow: He won the Premier League Golden Glove four times, a joint record for the most clean-sheet awards in the competition's history.
When Pep Guardiola took over Manchester City he wanted a keeper who played with his feet, so Hart was dropped and sent out on loan to Torino and then West Ham.
He rebuilt himself in Scotland, winning a domestic treble with Celtic in 2023 and lifting the Scottish Cup on the day he retired in 2024.

footballers.name: Gianluca Zambrotta
clues: I was born in Como and actually started out as a forward before being reinvented further back.
I won Serie A with two different clubs, Juventus and AC Milan.
I started the 2006 World Cup final, the night Zinedine Zidane was sent off for a headbutt.
I left Italy for Barcelona in 2006, moving alongside my defensive teammate Lilian Thuram.
I was a two-footed Italian full-back who won the 2006 World Cup.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 19th of February 1977. I played 98 times for my country, scoring twice.
footballers.story: A right winger who found his calling going the other way, Zambrotta became one of the most complete full-backs of his era, equally lethal down either flank because he was genuinely two-footed. He powered Juventus to back-to-back Scudetti before Calciopoli scattered the squad, following Lilian Thuram to Barcelona for two seasons in Catalonia. Later he added a Serie A title with Milan. But nothing tops the summer of 2006, when Italy lifted the World Cup in Berlin and Zambrotta, tireless up and down the touchline, was named in the tournament's team of the competition.
didYouKnow: He started out as a forward and then a right winger, only later reinventing himself as a full-back.
He scored Italy's 6th-minute opener against Ukraine in the 2006 World Cup quarter-final, a 3-0 win in Hamburg.
When Calciopoli relegated Juventus in 2006, he moved to Barcelona alongside former teammate Lilian Thuram.

footballers.name: Rickie Lambert
clues: I won back-to-back promotions in the English football divisions.
On my international debut I came off the bench and scored with my very first touch.
As a teenager scraping by between clubs, I once took a job in a factory bottling beetroot.
In 2014 I signed for Liverpool, the club I had supported since boyhood.
I became the talismanic striker and top scorer at Southampton.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 16th of February 1982. I played 11 times for my country, scoring 3 goals.
footballers.story: Rickie Lambert built his career the hard way, packing beetroot in a factory as a teenager after being released by Liverpool, then grinding through the lower leagues at Blackpool, Rochdale and Bristol Rovers. Southampton signed him in 2009, and from there the goals never stopped: a Football League Trophy at Wembley, back-to-back promotions and a Championship Golden Boot carried him all the way to the Premier League. His finishing was a craft in itself, free-kicks curled home and penalties dispatched with the calm of a man who had waited years for the stage. At 31 he finally earned an England call-up, and on his debut against Scotland he headed in the winner with his very first touch. A boyhood dream with Liverpool followed, closing a circle few could have imagined.
didYouKnow: As a teenager he worked in a beetroot-packing factory after being let go, years before he made it as a professional.
He climbed all the way from League One to the Premier League with Southampton, firing them through back-to-back promotions.
On his England debut against Scotland in 2013 he scored with his very first touch, heading in the winner moments after coming on.

footballers.name: Dietmar Hamann
clues: I scored the very last goal at the old Wembley before it was knocked down, a free-kick against England.
I won the Champions League with an English club.
I scored a penalty in that game after coming on at half-time.
I played for Newcastle, Liverpool, Manchester City and Bolton in England.
I represented Germany at two World Cups.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 27th of August 1973. I played 59 times for my country, scoring 5 goals.
footballers.story: They called him Didi, and for a decade he was the quiet architect of other men's glory. A tall, unhurried Bavarian, Hamann sat at the base of midfield and made destruction look like grace, reading danger a beat before it arrived and starting moves with a pass no one had spotted. Bayern first, then Newcastle, before seven seasons at Liverpool where he anchored the 2001 treble side and became a cult hero on the Kop. His most famous night needs no introduction: sent on at half-time in Istanbul, he steadied a sinking ship and helped author the greatest comeback European football has seen. For Germany he was a World Cup regular, dependable and understated to the last.
didYouKnow: He scored the last-ever goal at the old Wembley, a 30-yard free-kick for Germany against England in October 2000.
He came on at half-time with Liverpool 3-0 down in the 2005 Champions League final and helped turn the tie around.
He calmly converted his spot-kick in that Istanbul shootout, part of Liverpool's fifth European Cup triumph.

footballers.name: Franck Ribery
clues: I lost a World Cup final on penalties.
I was named UEFA's Best Player in Europe in 2013, ahead of Ronaldo and Messi.
I set up the winning goal with a backheel in a Champions League final at Wembley.
I was half of a feared wing partnership nicknamed after the two of us.
I was the scar-faced French winger and Bayern Munich great of the 2010s.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 7th of April 1983. I played 81 times for my country, scoring 16 goals.
footballers.story: Franck Ribery arrived at football late and by the back roads, drifting through the lower leagues before Marseille and then a move to Bayern Munich that would define a generation. Over twelve seasons in Bavaria he became the club's beating heart, a left-footed tormentor who could glide inside a full-back and thread the pass no one else had seen. His crowning year was 2013, when Bayern swept up everything in sight and Ribery was named the best player in Europe. For France he was a mercurial talent across two World Cups, gifted, tireless and quietly proud of the boy who came from nothing.
didYouKnow: He was named UEFA Best Player in Europe for 2012/13, finishing comfortably clear of both Cristiano Ronaldo and Lionel Messi.
Alongside Arjen Robben he formed Bayern's famous wing pairing nicknamed "Robbery", one flying down each flank.
The scars on his face come from a car crash when he was two years old, an injury that needed around a hundred stitches.

footballers.name: Dion Dublin
clues: In the 1997-98 season I scored 18 Premier League goals.
I invented and sell my own box-drum instrument, called the Dube.
I enjoyed my best goalscoring years at Coventry City, and later turned out for Aston Villa, Leicester City and Norwich.
I was versatile enough to fill in at centre-back as well as lead the line.
Since 2015 I have presented the BBC property show Homes Under the Hammer.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 22nd of April 1969. I played 4 times for my country, without scoring.
footballers.story: Dion Dublin took the long way to the top, sharpening his teeth in the lower divisions at Cambridge before Manchester United came calling in 1992. Old Trafford never quite opened up for him, but Coventry set him free. There he grew into one of the Premier League's most complete centre-forwards, all aerial menace and clean, unfussy finishing, and he shared the 1998 Golden Boot at his peak. A club-record move to Aston Villa followed, along with spells wearing the armband and even filling in at centre-half. Four England caps felt like slim reward for a striker so consistently dangerous.
didYouKnow: He invented a hand-played percussion instrument called the Dube, a compact variation on the cajon that he has performed on live with bands.
After hanging up his boots he became a television presenter, best known as one of the faces of the BBC daytime property show Homes Under the Hammer.
His 18 goals in 1997-98 earned a share of the Premier League Golden Boot alongside Michael Owen and Chris Sutton.

footballers.name: Georginio Wijnaldum
clues: My first season in England was with Newcastle United in the Premier League.
I broke through at Feyenoord as one of the club's youngest ever players.
I came off the bench and scored twice in one of the greatest European comebacks.
In France I turned out for Paris Saint-Germain.
In 2019 I won the Champions League.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 11th of November 1990. I played 96 times for my country, scoring 28 goals.
footballers.story: Georginio Wijnaldum was the engine you only noticed once he stopped running, a Rotterdam midfielder who covered every blade of grass without ever seeming rushed. He broke into Feyenoord as a teenager, found his goalscoring peak at PSV, then survived a relegation season at Newcastle before Jurgen Klopp turned him into a Liverpool cornerstone. On the biggest night of all he came off the bench against Barcelona and scored twice in two second-half minutes, dragging Anfield through one of the great European comebacks. Quiet, tireless and endlessly reliable, he was the sort of player teammates adored and opponents underrated.
footballers.numbers: 28 goals in 96 caps for the Netherlands
didYouKnow: He came off the bench and scored twice in two minutes to help Liverpool overturn a 3-0 first-leg deficit against Barcelona in the 2019 Champions League semi-final.
He became the youngest player ever to appear for Feyenoord's first team when he debuted at 16 years and 148 days old in 2007.
He captained PSV to the 2014-15 Eredivisie title, the club's first league championship in seven years.

footballers.name: Andy Cole
clues: Later in my career I asked to be known by my full first name rather than the shorter version.
I was once Britain's most expensive player, in a deal that sent a winger the other way.
I scored 34 league goals in one season, a Premier League record I share with Alan Shearer.
I formed a celebrated strike partnership with Dwight Yorke.
I won five Premier League titles and the 1999 treble at Manchester United.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 15th of October 1971. I played 15 times for my country, scoring once.
footballers.story: They spent years arguing over how to say his name, but never over his finishing. Andy Cole exploded out of Newcastle with 34 league goals in a single season, a blur of movement and cold, instinctive touches inside the box. His British-record move to Old Trafford in 1995 raised eyebrows, yet the goals kept flowing, 121 of them in United red. Alongside Dwight Yorke he built a telepathic partnership that drove the Treble of 1999, all grins and give-and-goes. England never quite handed him the run he deserved, but at club level few poachers were so ruthless.
didYouKnow: His 34 league goals for Newcastle in 1993-94 stood as a Premier League single-season record he shares with Alan Shearer.
His 1995 switch from Newcastle to Manchester United was a British transfer record, with winger Keith Gillespie moving the other way as part of the deal.
His telepathic strike partnership with Dwight Yorke fired Manchester United to the historic Treble in 1999.

footballers.name: Deco
clues: I finished runner-up for the Ballon d'Or in the same year that I won the Champions League.
I later won the Premier League and FA Cup in a single season in England.
On my international debut I came off the bench and scored a free-kick to beat the nation of my birth.
I won league titles in three different countries.
I was a naturalised Portugal midfielder who won the Champions League with both Porto and Barcelona.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 27th of August 1977. I played 75 times for my country, scoring 5 goals.
footballers.story: Born in Sao Paulo, Deco could have chased a Brazil shirt, but Portugal is where his magic found a home. At Porto he pulled the strings for Jose Mourinho, dictating tempo with a low centre of gravity and a pass nobody else saw, and he ran the 2004 Champions League final so completely that the trophy felt inevitable. A year later he swapped one dynasty for another at Barcelona, adding a second European crown in 2006 alongside Ronaldinho and a teenage Messi. Two clubs, two continents of admirers, one unmistakable brain. Few playmakers of his era saw the game so far ahead.
didYouKnow: He is one of a select few to win the Champions League with two different clubs, Porto in 2004 and Barcelona in 2006.
Born in Sao Paulo, Brazil, he built his entire international career with Portugal, winning 75 caps.
He now works as sporting director at Barcelona, one of the clubs he starred for as a player.

footballers.name: Branislav Ivanovic
clues: I scored a winner in a Europa League final against Benfica.
I captained my national team, and for years I was its most-capped player.
I lifted the Premier League title three times.
I was a defender comfortable at both right-back and centre-back, known for chipping in with vital goals.
I spent nine years at Chelsea, where I became one of the club's greats.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 22nd of February 1984. I played 105 times for my country, scoring 13 goals.
footballers.story: Born in Sremska Mitrovica in 1984, Branislav Ivanovic arrived in England from Lokomotiv Moscow as an unheralded stopper and left as a genuine Chelsea great. Powerful, brave and deceptively good in the air, he could bolt down the right flank or marshal the centre, and he had a habit of turning up with goals that mattered most. None mattered more than the looping stoppage-time header that won the 2013 Europa League final in Amsterdam. He later added league titles in Russia with Zenit and spent more than a decade as Serbia's captain and record cap-holder, a quietly relentless defender who simply refused to lose.
didYouKnow: He scored the looping stoppage-time header that beat Benfica to win Chelsea the 2013 Europa League final in Amsterdam.
Equally at home at right-back or centre-back, he was famous for his aerial threat and a knack for scoring decisive goals.
He captained Serbia and was long their most-capped player, holding the record of 105 appearances until 2024.

footballers.name: Bobby Zamora
clues: I scored the winning goal in two separate Championship play-off finals, for two different clubs.
On a European run to a major final I scored in a famous comeback against Juventus and struck after about 25 seconds against Wolfsburg.
I joined Tottenham for a fee but barely scored in my season there before finding my level elsewhere in London.
I was a cult hero at Brighton, scoring around 83 goals, winning back-to-back promotions and earning a chant sung to the tune of 'That's Amore'.
I was a target man valued more for my hold-up play and link-up than for filling my boots with goals.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 16th of January 1981. I played twice for my country, without scoring.
footballers.story: A born finisher with a poacher's nerve and a target man's frame, Bobby Zamora first made his name as a lower-league phenomenon, plundering goals for fun at Brighton and firing the Seagulls to back-to-back promotions. The big stage suited him too. He struck the winner that took West Ham up in 2005, then spearheaded Fulham's improbable charge to the 2010 Europa League final. Yet it is one swing of his boot at Wembley that endures: a stoppage-time winner for ten-man QPR in 2014, worth a fortune and etched forever into play-off folklore. Two England caps barely capture a career built on moments that mattered.
didYouKnow: He is one of only a handful of players to score the winning goal in two separate promotion play-off finals, doing it for West Ham in 2005 and again for QPR in 2014.
His stoppage-time QPR winner against Derby in 2014, scored while his side were down to ten men, was voted Wembley Stadium's Moment of the Year.
During his first spell at Brighton he was a lower-league sensation, scoring more than 80 goals and winning back-to-back promotions as top scorer in both divisions.

footballers.name: Andrei Kanchelskis
clues: Alex Ferguson sold me at the peak of my form, a decision that surprised many.
I scored both goals on my first Merseyside derby, in Everton's win at Anfield.
My move to Rangers made me a record signing in Scottish football at the time.
I am often called the only player to have scored in the Manchester, Merseyside and Old Firm derbies.
Because of the country I was born in and its break-up, I represented three different national teams.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 23rd of January 1969. I played 59 times for my country, scoring 7 goals.
footballers.story: The blur down Manchester United's right flank belonged to a winger born in Soviet Kirovohrad, all sudden acceleration and cannonball finishing. Kanchelskis arrived in 1991 and became the heartbeat of Ferguson's early Premier League machine, terrorising full-backs on the counter. His 1994 hat-trick in a 5-0 demolition of Manchester City remains one of Old Trafford's great derby days. Sold at his peak, he dazzled at Everton, wrestled with injuries in Fiorentina's colours, then found silverware again at Rangers. Few wingers of the nineties carried such raw, breathtaking speed.
footballers.numbers: 7 goals in 59 caps for the USSR, CIS and Russia
didYouKnow: He is often called the only player to have scored in the Manchester, Merseyside and Old Firm derbies.
His hat-trick powered Manchester United's 5-0 rout of Manchester City in November 1994.
Alex Ferguson sold him to Everton in 1995 while he was arguably at the peak of his powers.

footballers.name: Adam Lallana
clues: I am a Champions League and a Premier League winner, winning both once.
I was born in St Albans, Hertfordshire.
I moved from Southampton for a reported £25 million.
My next move, back to the south coast, was on a free transfer.
I was a technical attacking midfielder prized for my close control.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 10th of May 1988. I played 34 times for my country, scoring 3 goals.
footballers.story: Adam Lallana was Southampton to his bones, a boy who came through the academy and grew up with the club as it climbed back from the third tier to the Premier League, wearing the captain's armband along the way. His game was all soft touches and quick feet, a playmaker who kept the ball on a string in tight spaces and made hurried football look unhurried. A move to Liverpool followed, and though injuries chipped away at his best years, he found a home in Jurgen Klopp's press and collected the medals that had eluded him. For England he was quietly influential, technical and busy, voted the country's Player of the Year in 2016. Brighton gave him a graceful late chapter close to where it all began.
didYouKnow: He is a Southampton academy graduate who captained the club and rose with them through the divisions to the Premier League.
He won both the Champions League and the Premier League during his time at Liverpool under Jurgen Klopp.
He was voted England's Player of the Year in 2016 after a standout run of performances for the national side.

footballers.name: Aymeric Laporte
clues: I was born and raised in France, yet I chose to play my international football for another country.
I have won a World Cup.
I am only the second France-born player ever to represent a famous Basque club.
I won five Premier League titles in England.
I was a title-winning centre-back for Manchester City.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 27th of May 1994. I played 54 times for my country, scoring twice.
footballers.story: Born and raised in the French Basque foothills of Agen, Aymeric Laporte grew up an Athletic Bilbao devotee, and the boyhood love won out over his passport when he chose to play for Spain. A cool, ball-playing centre-half with a left foot made for opening angles, he became one of Pep Guardiola's trusted builders at Manchester City, sweeping up title after title. He sealed a Premier League on the final day with a header against Brighton, part of an English clean sweep no side had managed before. After a Saudi detour with Al-Nassr he came home to Bilbao, and with Spain he added a European crown and a World Cup to a glittering collection.
honours: Premier League (Manchester City, five times: 2018, 2019, 2021, 2022 and 2023)
didYouKnow: Born and raised in France, he switched allegiance to play for Spain, whom he helped win Euro 2024 and the 2026 World Cup.
He won five Premier League titles during his years with Manchester City under Pep Guardiola.
He was part of the first domestic treble in English football, City's clean sweep of the Premier League, FA Cup and League Cup in 2019.

footballers.name: Alvaro Morata
clues: I have won league titles in three different countries.
I came through Real Madrid's academy and had two different spells at the club.
I captained my country to a European Championship victory.
I had two separate spells with Juventus.
I also spent time in the Premier League with Chelsea.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 23rd of October 1992. I played 87 times for my country, scoring 37 goals.
footballers.story: For a decade Alvaro Morata carried the loneliest job in Spanish football: leading the line for a nation that prized the pass above the finish. He was never the fashionable pick, forever cast as the striker Spain might one day replace, yet he kept turning up when it mattered. A serial winner from his earliest days, he collected titles at Real Madrid, Juventus and beyond, drifting between giants and always finding another medal. Then, in the summer of 2024, the doubted man became the captain, lifting the European Championship as Spain's leader. Vindication, at last, for a striker who simply refused to disappear.
didYouKnow: He captained Spain to the Euro 2024 title, lifting the trophy after a 2-1 win over England in the Berlin final.
He has won league titles in three different countries: La Liga in Spain, Serie A in Italy and the Super Lig in Turkey.
A serial returner, he had two separate spells at Real Madrid and two at Atletico Madrid across his career.

footballers.name: Danny Welbeck
clues: I made my England debut against the country my parents came from.
I am still playing in the Premier League, at one of the biggest clubs in the country.
I won an FA Cup at a London club and missed the final injured.
United let me go the same week they signed Falcao.
I am Brighton's all-time leading Premier League scorer.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 26th of November 1990. I played 42 times for my country, scoring 16 goals.
footballers.story: Manchester United sold him and he scored the winner that knocked them out of the FA Cup. Welbeck came through at Old Trafford, won two league titles, and was moved on to Arsenal at twenty three for a fee that looked small even then. He gave Arsenal a Champions League hat-trick against Galatasaray, an FA Cup, and two serious injuries including an ankle that bent the wrong way at the Emirates. England kept picking him because the ball kept going in: sixteen goals in forty two caps, better than reputations suggest. Watford, then Brighton, where he was still scoring in the Premier League past thirty three.
didYouKnow: He scored a Champions League hat-trick for Arsenal against Galatasaray in 2014, the first treble of his career.
He scored the goal that knocked his former club Manchester United out of the FA Cup at Old Trafford in 2015.
He became Brighton's all time leading Premier League scorer before joining Chelsea in 2026.

footballers.name: Raul
clues: I scored at the Camp Nou and put my finger to my lips.
I was runner up for the Ballon d'Or in 2001.
I fell out with my national manager over squad rules and never played for my country again, which was poorly timed, because they won the next three major tournaments without me.
I won the Champions League three times.
Fernando Hierro called me the Ferrari, and I kissed my wedding ring when I scored.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 27th of June 1977. I played 102 times for my country, scoring 44 goals.
footballers.story: Real Madrid's record goalscorer for most of the modern era, and a man Atletico let slip across the city. Raul was in Atletico's academy when they shut it down, so he walked into Real Madrid instead and scored three hundred and twenty three goals for them, a record that only Cristiano Ronaldo has beaten. Six league titles and three Champions Leagues. For Spain he has a hundred and two caps and forty four goals, and not one trophy, because he belonged to the generation immediately before the good one and retired from international football just too early. Schalke and New York afterwards. He manages now.
didYouKnow: He came through Atletico Madrid's youth system and only joined Real Madrid because Atletico's president shut the academy to save money.
He made 741 appearances for Real Madrid, a club record, scoring 323 goals.
He was never sent off in his entire professional career.

footballers.name: Fabian Delph
clues: I was Aston Villa's player of the year two seasons running, and that is the biggest award I ever won.
I won the Premier League twice, playing in a new position.
I played for England in the 2018 World Cup.
I ended my career at Everton.
I was a Leeds academy midfielder who ended up playing left-back for Pep Guardiola.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 21st of November 1989. I played 20 times for my country, scoring 0 goals.
footballers.story: He told the cameras he was not going anywhere, and was a Manchester City player within the week. Delph was Aston Villa's captain and best midfielder, and the move made him a figure of fun before it made him a champion twice over. He had the better of the deal: two Premier League titles, and a season where Pep Guardiola turned him into a left-back and it worked. England took him to a World Cup semi-final, and sent him home mid-tournament for the birth of his daughter before he flew straight back out. Twenty caps, a long injury list, and a knack for being useful in whatever role was going.
didYouKnow: He captained Aston Villa in the 2015 FA Cup final, which they lost four nil to Arsenal.
He said publicly he would stay and captain Aston Villa, then signed for Manchester City six days later.
An injury to Benjamin Mendy turned him into Manchester City's first choice left-back during their record breaking 2017-18 season.

footballers.name: Juninho Pernambucano
clues: I beat Oliver Kahn from distance with a free kick, and that is the goal that made my name in Europe.
I won seven league titles in a row with a club that had never won one before I arrived.
I went to court to get out of my contract so I could leave Brazil.
I have scored more than seventy goals direct from free kicks, and plenty say nobody ever hit them better.
I am the Brazilian free-kick specialist of Lyon, and I later became their sporting director.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 30th of January 1975. I played 40 times for my country, scoring 6 goals.
footballers.story: The greatest free-kick taker who has ever lived, and it is not really a debate. Juninho scored around seventy five of them, from distances that should be impossible, with a technique he worked out himself by striking the ball on the valve. He won seven consecutive league titles at Lyon and is the club's record scorer from midfield. Brazil gave him only forty caps because the competition in that era was brutal, and he played at a World Cup. Vasco da Gama before and after. Cristiano Ronaldo and Gareth Bale both studied his technique. Nobody has ever matched it.
honours: Campeonato Brasileiro Serie A (Vasco da Gama, 1997)
Campeonato Brasileiro Serie A (Vasco da Gama, 2000)
didYouKnow: He scored more than seventy career goals direct from free kicks and is widely rated the finest free-kick taker the game has seen.
He developed the knuckleball free kick, struck with almost no spin so the ball moves unpredictably in flight.
He beat Oliver Kahn with a dipping long range free kick for Lyon against Bayern Munich.

footballers.name: Les Ferdinand
clues: I was a painter and decorator playing non-league when a London club took a chance on me.
My cousin captained England and won the Champions League.
I came off the bench in Alan Shearer's testimonial to a huge ovation, and then won the penalty he scored with the last kick of his career.
I was a record signing for Newcastle and scored twenty nine goals in my first season there.
I also played for Spurs, West Ham, Leicester, Bolton and Watford.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 8th of December 1966. I played 17 times for my country, scoring 5 goals.
footballers.story: Sir Les, from Hayes in the Isthmian League to the Premier League Player of the Year. Ferdinand was a late starter who got better the longer he went on: Queens Park Rangers made him, Newcastle made him famous during the Keegan years, and Tottenham got the elegant later period, including the ten thousandth goal in Premier League history. Seventeen England caps, and no tournament to show for them. He is a director of football at the club where he began now. There are three Ferdinands in the professional game and he was the first, which is worth remembering.
didYouKnow: He scored the ten thousandth goal in Premier League history, for Tottenham against Fulham in December 2001.
He is a second cousin of the football playing brothers Rio and Anton Ferdinand.
He was a painter and decorator playing non-league football for Hayes before QPR signed him.

footballers.name: Angel Di Maria
clues: I scored in four different finals for my country, including the winner at an Olympics.
I was the most expensive signing a British club had ever made, and I left a year later for fifteen million less.
They call me Noodle, because of how thin I am.
I am the leading Argentine assist provider in Champions League history.
I wore the number seven at Manchester United for one season and it did not go well.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 14th of February 1988. I played 145 times for my country, scoring 31 goals.
footballers.story: Man of the match in a Champions League final, and then the most expensive flop in British football. Di Maria left Real Madrid for Manchester United for a British record fee, lasted one season, and was gone to Paris. What makes him remarkable is what came after: he scored the winner in a Copa America final, scored in a Finalissima at Wembley, and scored in a World Cup final. Argentina spent a decade being told he was finished and he kept turning up in the games that mattered most. Over a hundred and forty caps and more than twenty goals. He went home to Rosario Central at the end, where he started.
didYouKnow: Manchester United signed him in 2014 for what was then a British record fee of almost sixty million pounds.
He scored in the 2021 Copa America final, the 2022 Finalissima and the 2022 World Cup final.
They call him Fideo, which means noodle, because of how slight he is.

footballers.name: Marco Materazzi
clues: I was sent off three times in a single season in England.
The most famous incidents involving me happened on a football pitch but had very little to do with the football being played.
I scored the equaliser in a World Cup final.
Zinedine Zidane said he would rather die than apologise to me.
I won the treble at Inter Milan.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 19th of August 1973. I played 41 times for my country, scoring 2 goals.
footballers.story: He scored the equaliser in a World Cup final and then got headbutted in the chest in front of the world. Materazzi's 2006 is the most famous thing about him and it should not be: he also converted a penalty in the shootout that won it. He spent a decade at Inter, winning a Champions League and five league titles, and was a defender of the old Italian school, which is to say that he fouled people. There was one season at Everton early on, which nobody remembers and he did not enjoy. Forty one caps. Perugia and Lazio before, and a great deal of noise throughout.
didYouKnow: He conceded the penalty and then scored Italy's equaliser in the 2006 World Cup final, and was headbutted by Zinedine Zidane in extra time.
He scored twelve goals for Perugia in 2000-01, a Serie A record for a defender in one season.
He spent the 1998-99 season in the Premier League with Everton before returning to Italy.

footballers.name: Santi Cazorla
clues: I was uncapped when they picked me for a European Championship, and we won it.
I took free kicks with either foot, and the stats had my shots almost exactly fifty fifty between the two.
I took Juan Roman Riquelme's record as Villarreal's highest scoring midfielder.
I scored the free kick that began a comeback in an FA Cup final and ended my club's nine year wait.
I won two FA Cups with Arsenal.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 13th of December 1984. I played 81 times for my country, scoring 15 goals.
footballers.story: He nearly lost his leg, and he came back and played for Spain again. Cazorla had an achilles tendon that became infected, needed somewhere around eight operations, and at one point the medical advice was about walking rather than football. He had already won two European Championships and two FA Cups and been the most two-footed player in England, able to cross and shoot equally well from either side, which almost nobody can genuinely do. Two years out, then back at Villarreal, then back in the national squad, aged thirty four. Eighty one caps. One of the game's most straightforwardly loved figures.
didYouKnow: An Achilles injury in 2016 became a gangrene infection that needed eight operations and put him at risk of amputation.
Surgeons grafted skin from his left forearm, where his daughter's name was tattooed, onto his infected heel.
He returned to his boyhood club Real Oviedo on a minimal salary and helped them back to La Liga.

footballers.name: Patrick Bamford
clues: I was offered a place at Harvard and a place in their football team, and I turned both down.
I was on Chelsea's books for five years, never played a game for them, and went out on loan seven times.
I went to a fee-paying school with no football team, so I played rugby at full-back until I was fifteen.
I scored my first career hat-trick against Leeds and signed for them four months later.
I scored seventeen Premier League goals in my first season with a newly promoted Leeds.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 5th of September 1993. I played 1 times for my country, scoring 0 goals.
footballers.story: Seventeen Premier League goals in a season, and one England cap to show for everything. Bamford spent his early twenties on loan from Chelsea to half the Championship without ever playing a minute for them, was voted the best player in that division, and finally found a home at Leeds, where Marcelo Bielsa made him into a genuine top-flight centre-forward. He got promoted, had the best season of his life, and then injuries arrived and took the rest of it. He is one of the game's more thoughtful figures, outspoken on mental health and on the environment, and happy to say so when it would be easier not to.
didYouKnow: He turned down a place at Harvard University, and a place in their football team, to stay in English football.
He had seven separate loan spells during five years as a Chelsea player and never made a competitive appearance for them.
He scored seventeen Premier League goals for a newly promoted Leeds in 2020-21.

footballers.name: Pablo Zabaleta
clues: I lost a World Cup final and a Copa America final, and won an Olympic gold.
I scored the first goal on the day my club won their first league title in forty four years.
I signed for my club one day before Abu Dhabi bought it.
I also played for West Ham.
I was a right back.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 16th of January 1985. I played 58 times for my country, scoring 0 goals.
footballers.story: The warrior, and the most popular right-back Manchester City have had. Zabaleta arrived from Espanyol in the last hours of the window on the day the club was taken over, which means he saw the whole thing from the beginning: two Premier League titles, including the one decided in the final seconds of the final day, and nine years of running into people slightly harder than was necessary. Argentina picked him fifty eight times, won Olympic gold with him and lost a World Cup final with him. West Ham got the last two years. He never scored for his country, which nobody held against him.
didYouKnow: He scored the opening goal in the win over Queens Park Rangers that clinched Manchester City the 2012 title.
He signed for Manchester City one day before the club was bought by Abu Dhabi.
He was sent off in the 2013 FA Cup final, only the third player ever dismissed in one.

footballers.name: Laurent Robert
clues: I equalled David Beckham's record for free-kick goals in a single Premier League season.
I won nine caps for France and not one of them came at a World Cup or a European Championship.
I was fined a hundred and eighty thousand pounds for criticising my manager in public, and that manager was Graeme Souness.
I played for Newcastle and then on loan at Portsmouth, and I never won a thing at club level.
I am the French left winger who gave Newcastle five years and hit free kicks for a living.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 21st of May 1975. I played 9 times for my country, scoring 1 goal.
footballers.story: A left foot that could do absolutely anything, attached to a man who did not fancy defending. Robert was Newcastle's winger through the Bobby Robson years and hit some of the best goals the club has seen, from free kicks and from thirty yards, and he fell out spectacularly with Graeme Souness when Souness asked him to track back. He went to Portsmouth, Benfica and eventually Australia. France capped him nine times. He is the exact type of footballer the Premier League has largely stopped signing: thrilling, selfish, and worth the ticket on his own.
didYouKnow: He was the first player from the island of Reunion to represent France.
He scored five free-kick goals in the 2001-02 Premier League season, matching David Beckham's single season record.
Newcastle fined him around a hundred and eighty thousand pounds after he criticised Graeme Souness in the press.

footballers.name: Jermaine Beckford
clues: I could have played for England, Jamaica or Grenada, and I chose Jamaica.
I scored the goal that knocked Manchester United out of the FA Cup in the third round, the earliest Alex Ferguson had ever gone out.
I played for Leeds, and years later went on loan to Huddersfield.
I scored against both Liverpool at Anfield and Chelsea at Goodison in my one Premier League season.
I am a television pundit now, and my brother won Wayne Rooney's Street Striker.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 9th of December 1983. I played 6 times for my country, scoring 1 goal.
footballers.story: He scored the goal that knocked Manchester United out of the FA Cup in the third round, the earliest Alex Ferguson had ever gone out. Beckford was a Leeds player in the third tier at the time, which made it worse. He could have played for England, Jamaica or Grenada and chose Jamaica. His one Premier League season brought goals at Anfield and against Chelsea at Goodison, and after that he dropped back down the leagues and kept scoring. He is a pundit now. His brother won a television football competition, which is the kind of detail that makes a family story rather than a career.
didYouKnow: He scored the only goal as League One Leeds knocked Manchester United out of the FA Cup third round in 2010.
He scored a hat-trick in the 2015 League One play-off final at Wembley to win Preston promotion.
He worked as a windscreen fitter for the RAC while playing non-league football for Wealdstone.

footballers.name: James Ward-Prowse
clues: I was the first midfielder to play every single minute of two consecutive Premier League seasons.
I was born in Portsmouth to Portsmouth-supporting parents and joined Southampton at eight.
Pep Guardiola called me the best free-kick taker he had ever seen.
I have scored more away free kicks in the Premier League than David Beckham.
I do a golf swing when I score, and I have gone back to Southampton.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 1st of November 1994. I played 11 times for my country, scoring 2 goals.
footballers.story: The best set-piece taker England has produced since David Beckham, and the numbers say so. Ward-Prowse has scored more Premier League free kicks than anyone except Beckham, and he built an entire top-flight career on it while captaining Southampton through some grim seasons. He did it without ever winning a trophy, which is the price of loyalty at a club like that. England gave him eleven caps and no tournament. There is more to him than free kicks, including a remarkable record for never missing a game, but the free kicks are why anyone outside Hampshire knows his name. West Ham, then Nottingham Forest.
didYouKnow: He has scored more away free kicks in the Premier League than David Beckham.
He was the first midfielder to play every minute of two consecutive Premier League seasons.
Pep Guardiola called him the best free-kick taker he had ever seen.

footballers.name: Dida
clues: I saved three penalties in a European Cup final.
I am a World Cup winner who did not play a minute of the tournament.
I was the first Brazilian goalkeeper nominated for the Ballon d'Or, and I finished second in the world goalkeeper vote in 2005.
Andriy Shevchenko said I was the first man he embraced after scoring his penalty against Buffon.
I played volleyball before football, and I helped break a prejudice about black goalkeepers in Brazil.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 7th of October 1973. I played 91 times for my country, scoring 0 goals.
footballers.story: Three saved penalties in a Champions League final shootout. Dida was AC Milan's goalkeeper across the great Ancelotti era and won two European Cups, the first on a night in Manchester where he was simply unbeatable from twelve yards. He was in Brazil's squad when they won the World Cup, without playing a minute of it. He is remembered in Britain for something else entirely: a Celtic supporter ran on and brushed past him, and he went down as though shot, which earned him a ban and a lot of jokes. Ninety one caps. Still one of the most decorated goalkeepers of the century.
didYouKnow: He saved three penalties in the 2003 Champions League final shootout against Juventus.
He is the only player to appear in five Confederations Cups, and leads the competition for appearances and clean sheets.
In 2006 he became the first black goalkeeper in fifty six years to start a World Cup match for Brazil.

footballers.name: Antonio Valencia
clues: I topped the public vote for best young player at a World Cup and the award went to Lukas Podolski.
I held the record for Premier League appearances by a South American.
I lost a Champions League final at Wembley to Barcelona.
I took the number seven after Cantona, Beckham and Ronaldo, then asked to give it back.
I went from Wigan to Manchester United and stayed ten years.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 4th of August 1985. I played 99 times for my country, scoring 11 goals.
footballers.story: Ecuador's finest export, and the only man brave enough to take the number seven shirt after Cristiano Ronaldo. Valencia came from Wigan, where he had been the best winger in the league that nobody talked about, and the shirt crushed him for a season. He handed it back, took twenty five, and became indispensable. Then Jose Mourinho turned him into a right-back and he was arguably better again, winning Manchester United's players' player award and eventually the club captaincy. Two Premier League titles, a Europa League, ninety nine caps and a World Cup for Ecuador. He finished back at Quito, where nobody needs telling who he is.
didYouKnow: He grew up in poverty in Lago Agrio, helping his mother sell drinks outside the local stadium.
He left home at sixteen for El Nacional without telling his father, on a bus fare his brother paid for.
Alex Ferguson gave him the Manchester United number seven shirt in 2012, and he handed it back after one season.

footballers.name: John Carew
clues: I was the first black player to represent my country.
I won La Liga in 2001-02, but not with Real Madrid or Barcelona.
I am the six foot five Norwegian striker of Valencia, Lyon and Aston Villa.
I was signed by Aston Villa in a straight swap with Milan Baros.
I am a six foot five striker.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 5th of September 1979. I played 91 times for my country, scoring 24 goals.
footballers.story: Six foot five, Norwegian, and the first black player ever to represent his country. Carew was a problem nobody solved twice the same way: he knocked Arsenal out of Europe on two separate occasions for Valencia, won a La Liga title in Spain, and arrived at Aston Villa in a straight swap for Milan Baros. He scored his penalty in the 2001 Champions League final shootout and still went home with nothing, the first of three finals he would lose. There is a second act too, stranger than the first. He acts now, and played a jungle warrior opposite Angelina Jolie. Ninety one caps, twenty four goals, and a career that was never once boring.
didYouKnow: He was the first black player to represent Norway at senior level.
He has acted since retiring, including a role in Maleficent: Mistress of Evil opposite Angelina Jolie.
He knocked Arsenal out of the Champions League twice while playing for Valencia.

footballers.name: Phil Jagielka
clues: I played a hundred and thirty three league games in a row, including every minute of one season.
Neil Warnock said I would be world class at tiddlywinks.
I was called into a Euros squad only because Gareth Barry got injured.
I captained Everton for six years and played more than eight hundred senior games.
I was Sheffield United's player of the season three years running.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 17th of August 1982. I played 40 times for my country, scoring 3 goals.
footballers.story: He once kept goal for Sheffield United in the Premier League era because he was the designated emergency goalkeeper, and he kept a clean sheet. Jagielka then became Everton's captain and one of the most reliable centre-halves in the country for a decade, got forty England caps, and scored a stoppage-time equaliser in a Merseyside derby at Anfield that is still the loudest thing most Evertonians have heard. He missed a penalty in a European Championship shootout. He won nothing at all, not one trophy in a twenty year career, which happens to good defenders at good-but-not-great clubs more often than anyone admits.
didYouKnow: He made his Sheffield United debut while still a trainee and was given a professional contract the next day.
He played 133 consecutive league games for Sheffield United, including every minute of the 2006-07 season.
He was the first Everton player ever to captain England, and became their most capped England international.

footballers.name: Dirk Kuyt
clues: I lost a World Cup final and a Champions League final.
I arrived in England as a striker and spent most of my time there on the right wing.
I scored all three goals in a win over Manchester United, playing for one of their biggest rivals.
Rafael Benitez said you could call me Mr Duracell, because I was always running and always on the go.
I won league titles in Turkey and in the Netherlands, and never one in England.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 22nd of July 1980. I played 104 times for my country, scoring 24 goals.
footballers.story: Not the quickest, not the most skilful, and somehow always exactly where the ball was. Kuyt scored a hat-trick against Manchester United for Liverpool in which all three goals travelled a combined few yards, which is the perfect summary of him. He played a Champions League final and a World Cup final and lost both. The Netherlands picked him a hundred and four times. The best bit came last: he went home to Feyenoord and won the league title in his final season, scoring a hat-trick on the final day to do it. One hundred per cent effort, every single week, for twenty years.
didYouKnow: He scored a hat-trick on the final day of 2016-17 to win Feyenoord their first title in eighteen years, then retired three days later.
He scored Liverpool's goal in the 2007 Champions League final, a 2-1 defeat to AC Milan.
He scored a hat-trick against Manchester United at Anfield in March 2011.

footballers.name: Nemanja Matic
clues: The same manager signed me at three different clubs.
Chelsea bought me for one and a half million, sold me as part of the deal for David Luiz, then paid fourteen times that to get me back.
I won two Premier League titles at Chelsea, but I made more Premier League appearances for another of the big clubs, only just.
I played youth football for both Red Star Belgrade and Partizan.
I scored Manchester United's goal of the season in 2017-18.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 1st of August 1988. I played 48 times for my country, scoring 2 goals.
footballers.story: Chelsea sold him, then bought him back for roughly ten times the money. Matic went to Benfica as part of a deal for David Luiz, became one of the best midfielders in Europe there, and Chelsea paid up to correct their own mistake. He won two Premier League titles with them and scored a volley in an FA Cup semi-final at Wembley that no defensive midfielder has any business hitting. Manchester United, Roma, Rennes and Lyon followed. He retired from international football early and still finished with close to fifty caps for Serbia. Enormous, calm, and almost impossible to hurry.
didYouKnow: He joined Benfica in 2011 as part of the deal that took David Luiz to Chelsea, and Chelsea bought him back three years later.
Benfica converted him from a playmaker into a defensive midfielder under Jorge Jesus.
His half volley against Crystal Palace in 2018 was voted Manchester United's goal of the season.

footballers.name: Diego Milito
clues: My brother played for Barcelona, and I scored four goals against Real Madrid in a single cup tie.
I scored both goals in a Champions League final and was named man of the match.
I had two separate spells at the same Italian club before the big move finally came.
I spent three years in Spain and won nothing, then won four trophies in a single season in Italy.
I am now the president of the Argentine club where I started and finished.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 12th of June 1979. I played 25 times for my country, scoring 4 goals.
footballers.story: They called him El Principe, and on one night in Madrid he played like one. Milito scored both goals in the 2010 Champions League final and was named man of the match, the centrepiece of a season that brought Inter four trophies. He had done something stranger four years earlier, putting four past Real Madrid in a single cup tie while playing for Zaragoza. Three years in Spain brought him nothing at all. He had two separate spells at Genoa before the big move came, won twenty five caps in total for a man with over two hundred club goals, and is now president of the Argentine club where he began and finished.
didYouKnow: He scored both goals in the 2010 Champions League final against Bayern Munich and was named man of the match.
He put four goals past Real Madrid in a Copa del Rey semi-final for Real Zaragoza in 2006.
He has been president of Racing Club, where he began and finished his career, since December 2024.

footballers.name: Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain
clues: I was once the youngest Englishman to score in the Champions League.
I moved between two Premier League title rivals for thirty five million pounds.
I won a Premier League and a Champions League, as well as a Scottish league and cup double.
Knee injuries cost me a Euros and a World Cup, two years apart.
I grew up supporting Arsenal, played for them six years, and won my league titles elsewhere.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 15th of August 1993. I played 35 times for my country, scoring 7 goals.
footballers.story: Southampton's youngest ever first-team player, and for a while the most exciting teenager in England. The Ox cost Arsenal twelve million pounds at eighteen and spent seven years there collecting FA Cups and a reputation as a man who could play almost anywhere and settle nowhere. Liverpool made him a midfielder and he was flying when a knee gave way in a Champions League semi-final against Roma, costing him a year and a World Cup. He came back to win the title, and sat on the bench for the Champions League final he had helped them reach. His father played for England too. Thirty five caps, and then a late second act in Turkey and a league and cup double in Scotland, which is a better last chapter than the story looked like getting.
didYouKnow: He scored on his Champions League debut in 2011 and became the youngest Englishman to score in the competition, taking the record off Theo Walcott.
He returned from a severe knee injury exactly 366 days later, as a substitute against Huddersfield.
After changing his Liverpool shirt number he paid out of his own pocket to replace the shirts fans had already bought.

footballers.name: Victor Valdes
clues: I won the Champions League three times.
In all three Champions League finals, I beat an English club.
My one tournament appearance for Spain was a clean sheet against Nigeria.
I have played for two great clubs, Barcelona and Middlesbrough, as well as Manchester United.
I was in goal when Barcelona beat Real Madrid six two and five nil.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 14th of January 1982. I played 20 times for my country, scoring 0 goals.
footballers.story: Five Zamora trophies, three Champions Leagues, and almost nobody outside Catalonia rated him. Valdes was Barcelona's goalkeeper for the entire Guardiola era, kept more clean sheets than anyone in the club's history, and was constantly described as a weakness by people who had not watched him sweep up behind that high line. Spain capped him twenty times, and he was in the squads that won a World Cup and a European Championship without playing. Then a strange, short Manchester United spell that ended in a public row with the manager, and Standard Liege and Middlesbrough after that.
didYouKnow: He won the Zamora Trophy for La Liga's best defensive record five times, four of them in a row.
He was in the Spain squads that won the 2010 World Cup and Euro 2012 without playing a minute of either.
He beat Manchester United in two Champions League finals and then signed for them.

footballers.name: Juan Pablo Angel
clues: I arrived at River Plate billed as the next Hernan Crespo.
Bradley Wright-Phillips is the only man who has passed my goalscoring record in New York.
I was a club record signing for Aston Villa at nine and a half million pounds.
My surname means angel, and supporters used to wear wings for me.
I took a ninety per cent pay cut to go home, then won three league titles in a row.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 24th of October 1975. I played 33 times for my country, scoring 9 goals.
footballers.story: Aston Villa's best Colombian, and a man whose first season in England was almost unbearable. Angel arrived for a club record fee, his wife lost a baby, and he barely played. The second season he scored twenty three. He went on to be one of the most liked players in the club's modern history, and then did it all again in New York, where he was the first designated player signing that actually worked and scored freely in Major League Soccer. Thirty four caps for Colombia. River Plate before, Los Angeles and Atlanta after. Quiet, decent, and much better than the fee suggested.
didYouKnow: Aston Villa signed him in 2001 for a club record fee of around nine and a half million pounds.
He was the New York Red Bulls' all time leading scorer until Bradley Wright-Phillips passed his total.
He took a ninety per cent pay cut to return to Colombia and won three league titles in a row.

footballers.name: Kim Kallstrom
clues: I won two Ligue 1 titles with Lyon.
I played in five different countries.
I played three league games for an English club and came away with an FA Cup.
A back injury was found in my medical and the club signed me anyway, so I spent my first six weeks in rehab.
I am the Swedish midfielder who turned up at Arsenal on loan from Spartak Moscow.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 24th of August 1982. I played 131 times for my country, scoring 16 goals.
footballers.story: He arrived at Arsenal with a broken back, and left with an FA Cup. Kallstrom's loan from Spartak Moscow is one of the strangest in Premier League history: the medical found a fracture, Arsenal signed him anyway because they were desperate, and he played three league games in four months before collecting a winner's medal at Wembley. The rest of the career was substantial.
