Two Ligue 1 titles with Lyon, spells in five different countries, and a hundred and thirty one caps for Sweden, which puts him among their most capped players of all time. A beautiful striker of a ball when his spine allowed it.
didYouKnow: He arrived at Arsenal on loan in January 2014 with a cracked vertebra in his back and still won the FA Cup that season.
He converted a penalty in Arsenal's FA Cup semi-final shootout win over Wigan.
He is Sweden's fourth most capped player of all time.

footballers.name: Ricardo Quaresma
clues: I was given an award for being the worst player in the league, and the next season my club won the treble.
I inherited Luis Figo's number seven shirt.
My trademark was a bending shot with the outside of my right foot, and it has its own name.
Jose Mourinho said at Inter Milan that I had great talent but still had to learn to work for the team.
I scored a 117th minute winner in a knockout tie at a European Championship, in a tournament we would go on to win.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 26th of September 1983. I played 80 times for my country, scoring 10 goals.
footballers.story: Nobody has ever hit a ball quite like it. The trivela, struck with the outside of the right foot and bending away from the goalkeeper, was Quaresma's signature and his argument: that there is more than one way to play. Italy gave him an award for being the worst player in the league, and the following season his club won the treble. Jose Mourinho said he had the talent but still had to learn to work for the team. He inherited Luis Figo's number seven anyway. He sat through an entire European Championship without kicking a ball, then came back four years later and scored a hundred and seventeenth minute winner on the way to Portugal lifting the thing. Maddening, magnificent, entirely himself.
didYouKnow: He is famous for the trivela, a curling shot struck with the outside of his right foot.
He scored the extra time winner against Croatia at Euro 2016 and the decisive penalty in the quarter-final shootout against Poland.
He waited fifteen years after his first cap to appear at a World Cup, finally playing in 2018.

footballers.name: Kalvin Phillips
clues: I started every match of a European Championship, including a final we lost on penalties.
My manager apologised in public for calling me overweight.
I gave my first England shirt to Marcelo Bielsa.
I cost forty two million pounds and then went six hundred and forty five days between appearances for the club.
I was called the Yorkshire Pirlo.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 2nd of December 1995. I played 31 times for my country, scoring 1 goal.
footballers.story: They called him the Yorkshire Pirlo, and Pirlo himself agreed, calling him a bit of a regista. Phillips came through at Leeds, the hometown boy in a side Bielsa dragged back to the top division, and he gave his first England shirt to the manager who made him. He started every match of a European Championship, including the final England lost on penalties, and was voted his country's player of the year. Then a forty two million pound move to Manchester City, and the harder half of the story: six hundred and forty five days between appearances, a manager apologising in public for calling him overweight, and a succession of loans. The talent was never the question.
didYouKnow: Leeds supporters nicknamed him the Yorkshire Pirlo for his passing range from deep.
Marcelo Bielsa converted him from a box to box midfielder into a specialist defensive midfielder.
He gave his first England shirt to Bielsa, the manager who had made him.

footballers.name: Roy Makaay
clues: They called me Das Phantom, because I appeared out of nowhere.
I won the Golden Shoe for Deportivo La Coruna.
I scored a hat-trick against a German giant in the Champions League, and they then signed me for a club record fee.
I was kept out of my national side by Kluivert, Bergkamp and van Nistelrooy.
I was later a coach at Rangers.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 9th of March 1975. I played 43 times for my country, scoring 6 goals.
footballers.story: They called him Das Phantom because he appeared out of nowhere, and the clock agreed: ten and a bit seconds into a Champions League tie at Real Madrid, he had scored the fastest goal in the competition's history. Makaay won the European Golden Shoe at Deportivo La Coruna and remains their leading scorer of all time. He announced himself to Bayern Munich by putting a hat-trick past them, and they responded by paying a club record fee to make him theirs. For the Netherlands he was unlucky rather than unwanted, kept out by Kluivert, Bergkamp and van Nistelrooy, and he never played at a World Cup. He coaches now, including a spell at Rangers.
didYouKnow: He scored the fastest goal in Champions League history against Real Madrid in 2007, timed at 10.12 seconds.
He is still Deportivo La Coruna's all time leading scorer.
He scored a hat-trick on his Deportivo debut and another in the last professional match he ever played.

footballers.name: Kaka
clues: I nearly joined Manchester City for over a hundred million pounds, and fans gathered outside my house to stop me.
I am one of only a handful of men to win a World Cup, a European Cup and a Ballon d'Or.
I was the second biggest fee ever paid at the time I was transferred.
I was three nil up at half time in a European Cup final and lost it on penalties.
I am the Brazilian playmaker of Milan and Real Madrid, and I never played in the Premier League.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 22nd of April 1982. I played 92 times for my country, scoring 29 goals.
footballers.story: The last man to win the Ballon d'Or before Messi and Ronaldo took it over for a decade. Kaka's 2007 was close to perfect: he tore the Champions League apart almost single-handedly and Milan won it. He had been a World Cup winner at twenty, a squad player who barely featured, and he was in Brazil's team for years afterwards. A swimming pool accident as a teenager fractured a vertebra and nearly ended everything before it began, which he always described as the reason he played with the shirt reading that he belongs to Jesus. The Real Madrid move never worked. Ninety two caps, and universally liked.
didYouKnow: He fractured his spine in a swimming pool accident as a teenager and was warned he might never play again.
Real Madrid signed him from AC Milan in 2009 for around sixty seven million euros.
His nickname came from his younger brother, who could not pronounce Ricardo as a small child.

footballers.name: Fabrizio Ravanelli
clues: I won league titles with two different Italian clubs and never a trophy in England, France or Scotland.
I scored a hat-trick on my Premier League debut, finished the season with thirty one goals in all competitions, and we were relegated.
I was the best paid player in the league and I would not stop complaining about the training ground.
I scored in a European Cup final and three months later I was playing in the north east of England.
They called me the White Feather, because my hair went white young.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 11th of December 1968. I played 22 times for my country, scoring 8 goals.
footballers.story: The White Feather, named for the silver hair, who scored in a Champions League final and then signed for Middlesbrough. Ravanelli won the European Cup with Juventus in 1996 and three months later was in the north east of England, where he announced himself with a hat-trick against Liverpool on his debut. That season Boro reached two cup finals, lost both, and were relegated, which may be the most Middlesbrough sequence ever recorded. He went on to Marseille, Lazio and Derby. Twenty two caps for Italy. Always complaining, always scoring, and always with the shirt pulled over his face.
didYouKnow: His prematurely white hair earned him the nickname the White Feather.
He scored in the 1996 Champions League final and three months later was playing in the north east of England.
He scored a hat-trick on his Premier League debut for Middlesbrough against Liverpool.

footballers.name: Nicky Butt
clues: I walked out on my manager after he picked his own son ahead of me.
I was player of the year at my second club, and I captained them to a Championship title.
I scored in Eric Cantona's comeback match.
I started a European Cup final only because our captain was suspended, and I played every minute of it.
I won six league titles and every one of them was at Manchester United.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 21st of January 1975. I played 39 times for my country, scoring 0 goals.
footballers.story: The forgotten one of the Class of 92, and the one who started a European Cup final. Butt only played in Barcelona because Roy Keane was suspended, and he played every minute of it, which is a good enough career highlight for anybody. Six league titles, all at Manchester United, and a treble. He scored in Eric Cantona's comeback match. Afterwards he was player of the year at Newcastle and had spells at Birmingham and Hull, and he walked out on one manager over a selection he thought was indefensible. Thirty nine England caps, and not a goal in any of them.
didYouKnow: He came through Manchester United's academy as one of the Class of 92 alongside David Beckham and Paul Scholes.
He started the 1999 Champions League final because Roy Keane was suspended, and played every minute of it.
He finished his playing career in Hong Kong with South China.

footballers.name: Diego Costa
clues: I scored seven goals in my first four Premier League games, which nobody had managed before.
I have two caps for the country I was born in and twenty four for the one I chose.
I won the Premier League twice and La Liga twice.
A French newspaper named me the most hated footballer in the world.
I was named after an Argentine, my brother was named after a Brazilian, and I ended up playing for Spain.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 7th of October 1988. I played 24 times for my country, scoring 10 goals.
footballers.story: Born in Brazil, capped by Brazil, and then a Spain international. Costa made the switch after two friendlies and spent the rest of his career being the most disagreeable man on any pitch he stood on, in the way his managers loved and everyone else resented. He won a La Liga title with Atletico Madrid, two Premier Leagues with Chelsea, and found out he was being sold by text message. He went back to Atletico and won the league again. There was also a short, strange spell at Wolves at the end. Twenty four goals in Spain's shirt, and roughly the same number of enemies.
didYouKnow: His father named him after Diego Maradona, despite the rivalry between Brazil and Argentina.
He played two friendlies for Brazil in 2013 before switching his international allegiance to Spain.
Antonio Conte told him by text message in 2017 that he was no longer in Chelsea's plans.

footballers.name: Javier Saviola
clues: I was the youngest ever South American Footballer of the Year, and I beat a record of Maradona's to it.
I took Spanish citizenship so my club could get round the limit on foreign players.
I was the youngest man on Pele's list of the greatest living footballers.
I played for Barcelona and then for Real Madrid, and I only won a league title at one of them.
I had four managers in six years at Barcelona, and Louis van Gaal was one of them.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 11th of December 1981. I played 39 times for my country, scoring 11 goals.
footballers.story: El Conejo, the rabbit, and once the most exciting teenager in South America. Saviola was five foot six and electric, and Barcelona paid a fortune for him when he was nineteen, and then he spent six years mostly being loaned out and being almost good enough. He scored freely for River Plate before and for Benfica afterwards, which suggests the problem was Barcelona rather than him. Then he did something nobody does and joined Real Madrid, where he played even less. An Olympic gold medal, a World Youth Championship, and forty caps for Argentina. The potential was never fully cashed.
didYouKnow: Barcelona paid around fifteen million pounds to sign him from River Plate at nineteen.
He scored eleven goals in seven games as Argentina won the 2001 World Youth Championship, a tournament record.
He crossed one of football's great divides by joining Real Madrid after six years at Barcelona.

footballers.name: Emmanuel Eboue
clues: I was booed by my own supporters while I was playing for them, and I came off in tears.
Sven named me in a World Cup squad, but not an England one.
I played more than two hundred games for Arsenal.
I started a Champions League final in Paris and lost it.
I am the Ivorian right-back from the Arsenal side that lost the 2006 Champions League final.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 4th of June 1983. I played 79 times for my country, scoring 3 goals.
footballers.story: Booed by his own supporters, and then applauded by them for years afterwards. Eboue had an afternoon at the Emirates where every touch was jeered, and the manager took him off to protect him. He came back from it and won two FA Cups, played in a Champions League final, and was one of the most popular players in the dressing room. Ivory Coast's golden generation used him as a right-back and sometimes a winger, and he won over a hundred caps. The hardest part came later: a Turkish title at Galatasaray, then a ban, a divorce and a public account of losing everything that he told with remarkable honesty.
footballers.numbers: 3 goals in 79 caps for Ivory Coast
didYouKnow: He started for Arsenal in the 2006 Champions League final at the Stade de France.
A section of Arsenal's own supporters booed him during a home match against Wigan in December 2008.
He signed for Sunderland in 2016 but a one year ban meant he never played a competitive minute for them.

footballers.name: Daniel Sturridge
clues: I am the first Englishman to win the Champions League with two different English clubs.
Steven Gerrard's slip arguably cost me a league title.
I scored the winner against Wales at a European Championship.
I formed a fearsome front three with Suarez and Sterling.
I finished up at Trabzonspor and Perth Glory, and I am on Sky Sports now.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 1st of September 1989. I played 26 times for my country, scoring 8 goals.
footballers.story: The best strike partnership of the decade, and a career that could not hold itself together. Sturridge came through Manchester City, failed to break through at Chelsea, and then found Luis Suarez at Liverpool and scored twenty one league goals in a title race they lost by two points. He got England's winner against Wales at a European Championship. He also got a worldwide ban for breaching betting rules over information about his own transfer, which he always insisted was a conversation with family. Twenty six caps, a Champions League winner's medal from the bench, and the nagging sense of a player whose body never gave him a clear run.
didYouKnow: He scored eight goals in twelve appearances during a half season loan at Bolton Wanderers in 2011.
He was the first Englishman to win the Champions League with two different English clubs.
He ended his playing career in Australia with Perth Glory and has been a Sky Sports pundit since 2023.

footballers.name: Jaap Stam
clues: I won three league titles in England and never one in Italy or with Ajax.
I lost a European Cup final in Istanbul.
I was the most expensive defender in the world, and I gave up money of my own to make the deal happen.
My manager sold me after my autobiography came out, and years later he admitted it was a mistake.
I was banned for five months for a steroid.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 17th of July 1972. I played 67 times for my country, scoring 3 goals.
footballers.story: Alex Ferguson's biggest regret, by his own admission. Stam was the best centre-half in Europe during Manchester United's treble season, immovable and quick with it, and then he wrote an autobiography, and a few months later he was sold to Lazio. Ferguson later said it was the worst decision he ever made. Stam went on to Milan and Ajax and kept being excellent, won sixty seven caps for the Netherlands, and played in a World Cup semi-final. He managed Reading to a play-off final afterwards. The strange thing is that he was never actually dropped for football reasons, not once.
didYouKnow: Manchester United paid PSV around ten and a half million pounds for him in 1998, then a world record for a defender.
He was sold to Lazio in 2001 shortly after the publication of his controversial autobiography.
He later managed Reading and took them to the Championship play-off final in 2017.

footballers.name: Pascal Gross
clues: I scored my club's first ever Premier League goal.
I assisted four goals in one Bundesliga match, only the third man on record to do it.
I was my club's all-time Premier League top scorer until Danny Welbeck passed me.
I won a Premier League player of the month at thirty five, and I am back at Brighton.
I did not play for my country until I was thirty two.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 15th of June 1991. I played 19 times for my country, scoring 1 goal.
footballers.story: He scored Brighton's first ever Premier League goal, and then spent most of a decade being their best player. Gross came from Ingolstadt for a small fee and turned into the most intelligent attacking midfielder in the division that nobody outside the south coast discussed, which included a Premier League Player of the Month award in his mid thirties. He once assisted four goals in a single Bundesliga match, something only two men had managed before him. Germany did not cap him until he was thirty two, which is the most Pascal Gross fact imaginable. Nineteen caps, and a club record that took Danny Welbeck to beat.
didYouKnow: He scored Brighton's first ever Premier League goal, against West Bromwich Albion in September 2017.
He did not make his Germany debut until 2023, at the age of thirty two.
He wears long sleeved shirts because of a grass allergy.

footballers.name: Julio Cesar
clues: I have won a treble that included the Champions League.
I was man of the match in a World Cup last sixteen, and two games later we lost seven one.
I was one of four Champions League winners in a QPR squad that got relegated.
I dribbled out of my own box four nil down and my manager called me an idiot in public.
I am the Brazilian goalkeeper from Inter's treble who later turned up at QPR.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 3rd of September 1979. I played 87 times for my country, scoring 0 goals.
footballers.story: For two or three years he was simply the best goalkeeper in the world. Julio Cesar was Inter's goalkeeper in the treble season, won a Champions League, and collected individual awards from everyone who hands them out. Brazil picked him eighty seven times. He saved two penalties in a World Cup shootout on home soil and wept openly about it, and a week later he was the goalkeeper in the seven one. In between he had a season at Queens Park Rangers that ended in relegation and which he always spoke about generously. Flamengo, Benfica, Toronto. One of football's genuinely well-liked men.
didYouKnow: He kept goal for Inter's 2010 treble side under Jose Mourinho.
He holds Brazil's record for the longest run without conceding, 581 minutes.
He was registered to Chievo purely to get round a Serie A quota and never played a game for them.

footballers.name: Ian Wright
clues: I was the country's leading scorer one season and still did not make the squad for that summer's tournament.
I released a single co-written with one of the Pet Shop Boys.
I lost an FA Cup final in a replay with one London club, then won two with another.
I broke my club's all-time scoring record, and Thierry Henry took it off me eight years later.
I scored a hundred and twenty eight league goals for Arsenal, and then spent years on Match of the Day.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 3rd of November 1963. I played 33 times for my country, scoring 9 goals.
footballers.story: Non-league at twenty one, and Arsenal's record goalscorer by thirty four. Wright was rejected as a kid, worked on building sites, and was playing Sunday football for Greenwich Borough when Crystal Palace took a chance on him. He came off the bench in an FA Cup final and scored twice. Then Arsenal, where he won a Golden Boot, a league title and a hundred and eighty five goals, a record that stood until Thierry Henry passed it. Thirty three England caps and nine goals. He is a broadcaster now, and one of the best there has been, which is a second career almost as distinguished as the first.
honours: Football League Second Division play-offs (Crystal Palace, 1989)
didYouKnow: He was still playing non-league football for Greenwich Borough when Crystal Palace signed him at twenty one.
He came off the bench in the 1990 FA Cup final and scored twice against Manchester United.
He broke Cliff Bastin's Arsenal scoring record in 1997 and revealed a shirt reading Just Done It.

footballers.name: Joaquin
clues: I played twenty seasons in La Liga and never won it.
I scored the first hat-trick of my career at thirty eight, and it broke a record of Alfredo Di Stefano's.
I was the most expensive signing in Valencia's history when they bought me.
I share the record for the most La Liga appearances ever, with a goalkeeper.
I spent most of my career at Real Betis.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 21st of July 1981. I played 51 times for my country, scoring 4 goals.
footballers.story: One of the great one-club loves, interrupted by eleven years elsewhere. Joaquin came through at Real Betis, left for Valencia and Malaga and Fiorentina, and then came home and played until he was forty one, by which time he had made more Primera Division appearances than almost anyone in history. He scored a Copa del Rey winner, lifted the trophy as captain, and became the oldest player to score a La Liga hat-trick. Fifty one caps for Spain, two World Cups, and the misfortune of being a right winger in the exact years Spain had an embarrassment of them. Always smiling, always running.
didYouKnow: He is the oldest player ever to score a hat-trick in La Liga, aged 38, breaking a record held by Alfredo Di Stefano since 1964.
He equalled Andoni Zubizarreta's record of 622 appearances in the Spanish top division.
He won the Copa del Rey with Real Betis at forty, seventeen years after lifting the same trophy with them.

footballers.name: John O'Shea
clues: I went in goal in a Premier League game and saved a shot from my own international teammate.
I have fourteen winners' medals and hardly any individual awards.
I have won the Premier League five times and have been relegated twice.
Roy Keane tore into me in an interview the club refused to broadcast.
I am an Irish defender.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 30th of April 1981. I played 118 times for my country, scoring 3 goals.
footballers.story: A full-back, a centre-half, a midfielder, and once a goalkeeper, all at Manchester United. O'Shea played thirteen years there and won five league titles, a Champions League and a Club World Cup while never being anybody's first choice in any single position, which is a remarkable trick. He scored a last-minute winner at Anfield. He kept goal in a Premier League match when both keepers were unavailable, and he kept a clean sheet in it. One hundred and eighteen caps for Ireland, then Sunderland and Reading. The nutmeg on Luis Figo is still the clip people send each other.
footballers.numbers: 3 goals in 118 caps for Republic of Ireland
didYouKnow: He went in goal for Manchester United in 2007 after Edwin van der Sar was injured and all three substitutes had been used.
He scored a stoppage time winner at Anfield in March 2007 that proved pivotal in United's title win.
He served as interim manager of the Republic of Ireland in 2024.

footballers.name: Emmanuel Petit
clues: I scored in a World Cup final, and it was the thousandth goal in my federation's history.
I appeared as myself in a Christmas episode of The Bill.
The same manager signed me twice, nine years apart, at two different clubs.
I won the Double in my first season in England, and later lost an FA Cup final to that same club.
I played in Arsenal's midfield alongside Patrick Vieira, and later in Chelsea's alongside Frank Lampard.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 22nd of September 1970. I played 63 times for my country, scoring 6 goals.
footballers.story: A blond midfielder who scored the goal that ended a World Cup final. Petit's ball into the net at the Stade de France made it three nil, and he and Patrick Vieira went back to Arsenal having won the whole thing a few weeks after winning a Premier League and FA Cup double together. Add a European Championship two years later and he had, briefly, won everything worth winning. Barcelona took him for a single poor season, Chelsea got the rest. He grew up at Monaco. His career had the shape of an arrow: Highbury for the glory, and the summer of 1998 above everything.
didYouKnow: He scored France's third goal in the final minute of the 1998 World Cup final against Brazil.
He wore the number seventeen throughout his club career in tribute to his brother Olivier, who died at that age.
Arsene Wenger signed him twice, first for Monaco as a teenager and then for Arsenal nine years later.

footballers.name: Peter Crouch
clues: I took the Premier League record for substitute appearances off Shola Ameobi, and James Milner later took it off me.
I was my country's top scorer in a qualifying campaign and we still did not make the tournament.
I played for both Portsmouth and Southampton, and I did Portsmouth twice.
I hold the Premier League record for headed goals.
I was famous for my celebration as much as my goals.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 30th of January 1981. I played 42 times for my country, scoring 22 goals.
footballers.story: Six foot seven, and a better footballer than the joke allowed. Crouch played for eleven clubs, scored a hundred Premier League goals, and was particularly good at the thing nobody expected of a man that height, which was controlling the ball on the floor. For England he got twenty two goals in forty two games, a ratio most strikers would take, and did the robot celebration at a World Cup. He is as famous now for the podcast and the self-deprecation as for the football, which is a little unfair, because he was an excellent player for a very long time. The line about what he would be without football is immortal.
didYouKnow: He holds the record for the most headed goals in Premier League history.
He marked goals with a deliberately stiff robot dance that he first unveiled before the 2006 World Cup.
He played for both Portsmouth and Southampton, and had two separate spells at Portsmouth.

footballers.name: Fabio Quagliarella
clues: I equalled a scoring record that Gabriel Batistuta had set back in 1994.
I played my whole career in Italy, for eight different clubs.
I captained Sampdoria and finished my career there.
I won three league titles in a row without ever really being first choice.
I left my hometown club for their biggest rivals, and it took seven years for anyone to find out why.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 31st of January 1983. I played 28 times for my country, scoring 9 goals.
footballers.story: Serie A's top scorer at thirty six years old. Quagliarella scored in eleven consecutive league games that season, equalling a record held by Gabriel Batistuta, and won the Golden Boot about fifteen years later than anyone expected him to. The reason his career wandered through Udinese, Napoli, Juventus, Torino and Sampdoria is darker than restlessness: a stalker spent years sending threats to him and his family, and he left his hometown club without ever being able to explain why. The truth came out long afterwards and the apologies arrived with it. Twenty eight caps for Italy, and a late flowering that nobody begrudged him.
didYouKnow: He was Serie A's top scorer in 2018-19 with twenty six goals, at the age of thirty six.
He equalled Gabriel Batistuta's record by scoring in eleven consecutive Serie A matches.
He left his home city club Napoli after he and his family were threatened by a stalker over five years.

footballers.name: Mark Noble
clues: I scored twenty eight Premier League penalties and missed only five.
I had Irish grandparents and I turned down the chance to play for Ireland, because I thought a kid who had dreamed of it deserved it more than me.
My club renamed their young player of the year award after me.
I had retired and taken a desk job at the club when Declan Rice walked a European trophy over and handed it to me to lift.
Sam Allardyce said I looked five foot eight but stood six foot four every time I pulled the shirt on.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 8th of May 1987. I was never capped by my country.
footballers.story: Seventeen years, five hundred and fifty appearances, one club, and not a single England cap. Noble was West Ham, in every sense: a local boy who captained them, got them promoted twice, and stayed through every version of the club including the move away from the ground he grew up next to. He was a proper midfielder, a reliable penalty taker, and the symbol of something the Premier League has almost run out of. The last act was a substitution brought on specifically to take a penalty against Manchester United, and he missed it, which somehow made everyone love him more. He is the sporting director now.
honours: Football League Championship play-offs (West Ham United, 2005)
Football League Championship play-offs (West Ham United, 2012)
didYouKnow: He was never capped by England at senior level, despite eighteen years as a professional and twenty under-21 appearances.
He made 550 appearances for West Ham United and was club captain for seven years.
He returned to West Ham as the club's sporting director in January 2023.

footballers.name: Jimmy Floyd Hasselbaink
clues: I started out as a goalkeeper and ended up winning two Golden Boots.
The manager who released me from Middlesbrough hired me as an England coach many years later.
I went from Leeds to Chelsea by way of Spain, for a club record fee.
I was born in Suriname, played for the Netherlands, and I went back to coach Suriname.
The manager who signed me at Atletico Madrid turned up as my Chelsea boss a few months after I got there.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 27th of March 1972. I played 23 times for my country, scoring 9 goals.
footballers.story: He hit a football harder than almost anyone, and he scored wherever he went. Hasselbaink won the Premier League Golden Boot at Leeds, left for Atletico Madrid and got relegated with them while being their top scorer, then came back and won another Golden Boot at Chelsea. He is one of very few men to have shared the award twice with different clubs. Born in Suriname, raised in the Netherlands, he played at a World Cup and a European Championship. Middlesbrough and Charlton came at the end. He has managed since, with mixed results, and remains a man whose shooting you simply do not forget.
didYouKnow: He was born in Paramaribo, Suriname, and moved to the Netherlands at the age of five.
He won the Premier League Golden Boot twice, shared with Leeds in 1999 and outright with Chelsea in 2001.
He started out playing in goal as a boy before moving to winger and then forward.

footballers.name: Jens Lehmann
clues: I was in a World Cup final squad and never got on the pitch, because the man ahead of me was the best in the world.
I was voted the best goalkeeper in Europe twice, nine years apart.
I went eight hundred and fifty three minutes without conceding in the Champions League, then got sent off in the final.
I went through a Premier League season without losing a game.
I am the German goalkeeper from Arsenal's Invincibles.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 10th of November 1969. I played 61 times for my country, scoring 0 goals.
footballers.story: Every minute of an unbeaten league season, and then sent off in a European Cup final. Lehmann was Arsenal's goalkeeper through the Invincibles and a man of magnificent contradictions: eight hundred and fifty three consecutive Champions League minutes without conceding, and also the club record for red cards at Borussia Dortmund by any player, not just any keeper. He won league titles in three different countries. He saved two penalties in a World Cup shootout against Argentina using notes hidden in his sock. He sat on the bench for a World Cup final behind Oliver Kahn, and was twice voted the best goalkeeper in Europe. Never dull, never quiet.
didYouKnow: He played every match of Arsenal's unbeaten 2003-04 Premier League season.
He is the only goalkeeper ever sent off in a European Cup final, dismissed against Barcelona in 2006.
He saved two penalties in Germany's 2006 World Cup shootout against Argentina using notes hidden in his sock.

footballers.name: Phil Neville
clues: I scored in the shoot-out that knocked my old club out of an FA Cup semi-final.
I captained England at cricket as a boy, and I was the youngest player ever to turn out for Lancashire's second eleven.
I was naturally right footed and spent years filling in at left-back.
I won six league titles at one club and nothing at all in eight years at the next.
My brother and I were the first siblings ever to captain opposing Premier League sides.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 21st of January 1977. I played 59 times for my country, scoring 0 goals.
footballers.story: Six league titles, fifty nine England caps, and zero goals for his country. Neville was the squad man who was somehow never quite a squad man, playing full-back on either side and in midfield for Manchester United across a decade of trophies, then captaining Everton for years afterwards. The one moment that followed him around was a penalty conceded against Romania that sent England out of a European Championship. He coached, then managed England's women to a World Cup semi-final, then went to Miami. His brother and his sister were both internationals too, in two different sports, which is an unusual family.
didYouKnow: He captained England Under-15s at cricket and is the youngest player ever to appear for Lancashire's second eleven.
He and his brother Gary were the first siblings to captain opposing Premier League sides.
He managed England's women's team to fourth place at the 2019 World Cup.

footballers.name: Christian Benteke
clues: I scored the fastest goal in World Cup history, qualifying included, after eight seconds.
I won the MLS Golden Boot with twenty three goals.
I scored twice at Anfield, and two and a half years later I signed for them.
My family fled a dictatorship when I was small and I grew up in Belgium.
I cost Liverpool thirty two and a half million and they sold me to Crystal Palace a year later.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 3rd of December 1990. I played 45 times for my country, scoring 18 goals.
footballers.story: Six foot three of Belgian nuisance, and briefly the most talked-about striker in England. Benteke arrived at Aston Villa and dragged a sinking club to safety almost on his own, which earned him a thirty two and a half million pound move to Liverpool. There he scored an overhead kick against Manchester United that was better than anything else in his season, and left after a year anyway. Crystal Palace got the long tail of his career, then Washington, where he won the MLS Golden Boot at thirty three. More than sixty caps for a golden generation, usually as the option they turned to when the clever football ran out.
didYouKnow: He scored the fastest goal in any World Cup match, qualifying included, after 8.1 seconds against Gibraltar in 2016.
He ruptured his Achilles in training in April 2014 and missed the World Cup as Belgium's expected first choice striker.
He won the MLS Golden Boot with D.C. United in 2024, scoring twenty three goals.

footballers.name: Oriol Romeu
clues: I was an unused substitute in the Munich final, and I still got a Champions League medal.
Pep Guardiola gave me my debut, and in that first spell I played one league game for them.
The only individual awards of my career all came in a single season at Southampton.
I won a La Liga title off one league appearance.
I am the Spanish defensive midfielder who ended up in Japan.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 24th of September 1991. I was never capped by my country.
footballers.story: A Barcelona boy who had to leave to have a career, and then got to go home. Romeu came through La Masia, could not get near the first team, and was sold to Chelsea at nineteen, where he was in the squad that won a Champions League. Southampton gave him six years and the holding role in front of the back four, where he was underrated to the point of invisibility. Then Girona played brilliantly with him in the side and Barcelona bought him back at thirty one, which almost never happens to anybody. Spain never capped him once. Not every good career needs an international record.
didYouKnow: He was never capped by the senior Spain side, playing only up to under twenty one level and four times for Catalonia.
He won a La Liga title off a single league appearance for Barcelona in 2010-11.
He won the Champions League and the FA Cup with Chelsea in his first season after leaving Barcelona.

footballers.name: Thomas Gravesen
clues: A training ground scuffle broke out after I tackled Robinho.
I left Everton for Real Madrid, and nobody saw it coming.
I retired at thirty two, made my money on investments, and now live down the road from Nicolas Cage.
I represented Denmark at Euro 2000, the 2002 World Cup and Euro 2004.
I won the Scottish double with Celtic.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 11th of March 1976. I played 66 times for my country, scoring 5 goals.
footballers.story: One of the strangest transfers of the modern era, and nobody saw it coming. Gravesen was a combative, shaven-headed midfielder having a perfectly good time at Everton when Real Madrid rang, and off he went to the Bernabeu to play alongside the Galacticos. Fabio Capello summed him up better than anyone, saying there would be no problems with him, he was just a little bit peculiar. He won nothing in Spain. The only trophies of his career came in Scotland, a domestic double with Celtic. He never won a single individual award. He retired at thirty two, made a fortune on investments, and now lives down the road from Nicolas Cage.
didYouKnow: Real Madrid signed him from Everton in January 2005 for about two and a half million pounds.
Mike Tyson asked him for his shirt after a 2002 World Cup qualifier against Iceland.
He made his money in investments after retiring and settled in a gated Los Angeles community near Nicolas Cage.

footballers.name: Teddy Sheringham
clues: I had never won a major trophy until I was thirty three, and then I won three in a single season.
I was the Premier League's first ever top scorer.
I am the oldest outfield player ever to appear in a Premier League match.
I played for Millwall and for West Ham, which did not make me popular in either place.
I scored the equaliser and set up the winner in a European Cup final, both in injury time.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 2nd of April 1966. I played 51 times for my country, scoring 11 goals.
footballers.story: He came on as a substitute in a European Cup final, scored the equaliser, and set up the winner in the next ninety seconds. Sheringham's treble season with Manchester United also included scoring in an FA Cup final, which is an absurd three weeks of work. Before that he had been Tottenham's best player for years and formed the England partnership with Alan Shearer that got them to a European Championship semi-final at home. Fifty one caps, eleven goals. He played in the Premier League until he was forty, which was a record for an outfield player, and he never looked like he was running.
honours: Football League Championship play-offs (West Ham United, 2005)
didYouKnow: He scored the equaliser and set up the winner in stoppage time of the 1999 Champions League final.
He is the oldest outfield player ever to appear in a Premier League match.
He was the top scorer in the inaugural Premier League season of 1992-93.

footballers.name: Hulk
clues: I won titles in Portugal, Russia, China and Brazil and never in a big five league.
I never played in England, and my Brazil debut was against them.
I spent three years in Japan, two of them in the second division, before anyone in Europe noticed.
My free kick won my club a Russian league title.
My father named me after a television series, because I was so strongly built.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 25th of July 1986. I played 49 times for my country, scoring 11 goals.
footballers.story: Named after a television programme by his own father, because of how strongly built he was. Hulk's career is the great argument for looking outside the obvious leagues: he won titles in Portugal, Russia, China and Brazil, and never played a minute in any of Europe's big five. Before any of that he spent three years in Japan, two of them in the second division, which is where he learned to hit a ball with that absurd left foot. A free kick of his won Zenit a Russian title. He played for Brazil, made his debut against England, and never played a club game in England. Sheer, unreasonable power.
didYouKnow: His nickname came from his father, a fan of the Incredible Hulk television series.
He scored thirty seven goals in forty two games on loan at Tokyo Verdy in Japan's second tier.
He has won league titles in Portugal, Russia, China and Brazil but never in a big five European league.

footballers.name: Hernan Crespo
clues: I was once the most expensive player in the world, and I never won a league title at that club.
I was signed by an Italian giant as a replacement for the Brazilian Ronaldo.
I played for both Milan clubs, and for Inter twice.
I scored thirty five goals for Argentina.
Claudio Ranieri signed me and Jose Mourinho loaned me out within a year.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 5th of July 1975. I played 64 times for my country, scoring 35 goals.
footballers.story: He scored in a Champions League final for a club that did not own him. Crespo was on loan at AC Milan from Chelsea on the night in Istanbul, and his backheel flick made it three nil at half time, which remains one of the loveliest goals ever scored in a final nobody won. His career was a procession of enormous fees: a world record for a defender's wage bill when Lazio bought him from Parma, then Inter, then Chelsea twice with two Italian loans in between. Serie A's top scorer in 2001, thirty five goals in sixty four games for Argentina, and he is a coach now. Elegant and ruthless at once.
didYouKnow: Lazio broke the world transfer record to sign him from Parma in 2000.
He scored twice for AC Milan in the 2005 Champions League final and still finished on the losing side.
He was the first player to score Champions League goals for five different clubs.

footballers.name: Per Mertesacker
clues: I won a World Cup and more than a hundred caps, and I never won a league title in any country.
I won three FA Cups with a London based Premier League club.
My nickname came from a Roald Dahl book, and I used it as the title of my autobiography.
I had three clubs in my whole career, and two of them were German.
I ran Arsenal's academy for eight years, and I am about to start a big job with the German federation.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 29th of September 1984. I played 104 times for my country, scoring 4 goals.
footballers.story: Six foot six, and sick with nerves before every single match. Mertesacker admitted long afterwards that he used to vomit before kick-off and spent his career dreading the thing he was best at, which makes a hundred and four caps and a World Cup winner's medal rather more impressive than they already were. At Arsenal he was the calmest man in a chaotic defence, and the story everyone tells is the FA Cup final he started having barely played all season, and won. He is the academy manager there now, which suits him exactly. The BFG, they called him, and he liked it.
didYouKnow: His blunt interview given from an ice bath at the 2014 World Cup became a viral sensation in Germany.
He captained Arsenal to victory in the 2017 FA Cup final having barely played all season through injury.
He took charge of Arsenal's academy immediately after retiring in 2018.

footballers.name: Leon Britton
clues: I made a hundred and forty one Premier League appearances and never scored in any of them.
I won a League Cup at Wembley with a club that had been in the bottom division not long before.
I was five foot four, and in 2011 I was statistically the best passer in the world, ahead of Xavi.
They gave me the freedom of the city of Swansea.
Supporters passed buckets round the ground to pay for my loan, and they called it the Battle For Britton.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 16th of September 1982. I was never capped by my country.
footballers.story: Five foot four, and in 2011 statistically the best passer in the world, ahead of Xavi. Britton went to Swansea when they were in the bottom division and still there when they were beating Manchester United, which is as complete a club story as English football has produced. He made a hundred and forty one Premier League appearances and never scored once. He won a League Cup at Wembley. The supporters once passed buckets round the ground to raise the money for his loan fee and called it the Battle For Britton. They gave him the freedom of the city in the end, and nobody argued.
didYouKnow: West Ham paid Arsenal four hundred thousand pounds for him at sixteen, the highest fee ever paid for a player that age at the time.
Swansea supporters part funded his 2002 loan with a bucket collection they called the Battle For Britton.
In 2011 he was the most accurate passer in world football among players with over a thousand passes, ahead of Xavi.

footballers.name: Ngolo Kante
clues: Arsenal passed on me twice and signed Granit Xhaka instead.
I used to get to training on a kick scooter, and I have an accounting diploma.
I am the first outfield player since Eric Cantona to win back-to-back English titles with different clubs.
I turned down Mali twice and never played for France at any youth level.
They say seventy per cent of the planet is covered by water and the rest by me.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 29th of March 1991. I played 69 times for my country, scoring 2 goals.
footballers.story: He won the Premier League, and then he won it again with somebody else. Kante was playing in the French third tier not long before Leicester City signed him, and he was the engine of the strangest title win in history, then moved to Chelsea and won the thing again the very next season. Add a World Cup, a Champions League in which he was man of the match in the final, a Europa League and a PFA Player of the Year award, and the only sensible conclusion is that he is the most quietly decorated footballer of his generation. He is famously modest, famously small, and famously everywhere.
didYouKnow: He was born in Paris to Malian parents and turned down an approach from Mali before the 2015 Africa Cup of Nations.
He won back to back Premier League titles with two different clubs, Leicester and Chelsea.
He was made a Knight of the Legion of Honour in 2018 after France won the World Cup.

footballers.name: Helder Postiga
clues: Glenn Hoddle signed me and called me a young player of proven ability.
I played at two World Cups and three European Championships for Portugal.
I chipped my penalty straight down the middle in a shootout against England.
I spent a season flopping at Tottenham and then knocked England out at that summer's Euros.
I am the Portuguese striker who won two league titles at Porto.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 2nd of August 1982. I played 71 times for my country, scoring 27 goals.
footballers.story: Written off in England, and then he scored against England. Postiga was a Tottenham signing who managed one league goal in a season and was sent home to Porto as a failure, and within weeks he chipped a quarter-final equaliser past David James at a European Championship and ran to the camera. He had the career Spurs never saw: Porto, Sporting, Panathinaikos, Zaragoza, Valencia and Lazio, and twenty seven goals in seventy one games for Portugal. He played in two World Cups and three European Championships, and reached a final. In England he is a punchline. In Portugal he is a man who kept turning up when it counted.
didYouKnow: Tottenham paid Porto over six million pounds for him in 2003 and he scored one league goal before being sold back.
He equalised against England in the Euro 2004 quarter-final and then converted a Panenka in the shootout.
He ended his career in India, winning the 2016 Indian Super League with Atletico de Kolkata.

footballers.name: Lomana LuaLua
clues: I scored against my own parent club while on loan, and the FA changed the rules because of it.
I played at four Africa Cup of Nations and captained my country, and I never played at a World Cup.
Bobby Robson signed me, then told the press I should keep my mouth shut and do what I was paid for.
I did seven back flips when I scored, and one of them injured me during a game against Arsenal.
My brother and two of my cousins all played professionally, and one of them is Yannick Bolasie.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 28th of December 1980. I played 31 times for my country, scoring 7 goals.
footballers.story: Seven back flips after every goal, and one of them injured him during a match against Arsenal. LuaLua was a Bobby Robson signing at Newcastle, where he was more entertainment than reliability, and the manager once told the press he should keep his mouth shut and do what he was paid for. He went to Portsmouth and then, on loan at Olympiacos, scored against Portsmouth, which was so obviously absurd that the rules were changed afterwards. Four Africa Cup of Nations and the captaincy of DR Congo, and never a World Cup. His brother and two of his cousins played professionally too, one of them Yannick Bolasie.
footballers.numbers: 7 goals in 31 caps for DR Congo
didYouKnow: He injured himself performing his trademark somersault celebration against Arsenal in 2006 and missed matches as a result.
His brother Kazenga and his cousins Yannick Bolasie and Tresor Kandol also became professional footballers.
He scored against his own parent club while on loan, and the FA changed the loan rules because of it.

footballers.name: Jack Rodwell
clues: I modelled the Great Britain kit for an Olympics and then was not picked for the squad.
One local paper called me the worst signing in my club's history, and another one agreed.
I captained the A-League All Stars against Barcelona.
I was signed by Manchester City for twelve million.
I am now probably most famous for my portrayal on Sunderland 'Til I Die, where I look like a right tosser.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 11th of March 1991. I played 3 times for my country, scoring 0 goals.
footballers.story: He modelled the Great Britain kit for an Olympics and then was not picked for the squad, which is a cruelly accurate summary. Rodwell was Everton's great hope, a centre-half who could play in midfield, and Manchester City paid twelve million for him on the strength of it. He played almost nothing. At Sunderland he became a byword for the worst kind of contract, one local paper calling him the worst signing in the club's history, and his portrayal in a documentary series did not help. Three England caps. He went to Australia and captained an All Stars team against Barcelona, which is a better ending than most people realise.
didYouKnow: He became Everton's youngest ever player in European competition, appearing against AZ Alkmaar at sixteen.
Manchester City paid Everton twelve million pounds for him in 2012, yet he made only sixteen league appearances in two seasons.
He finished his career in Australia, playing for both halves of the Sydney derby.

footballers.name: Dennis Bergkamp
clues: I was named after a Scottish striker, and my parents had to add a letter to the spelling to get it past the registrar.
An Italian newspaper renamed its donkey of the week award after me.
Bobby Robson said after one of my goals that you just had to accept I had done a beautiful thing.
I am the only Dutchman in the English Football Hall of Fame.
I was Arsenal's record signing in 1995 and I stayed eleven years.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 10th of May 1969. I played 79 times for my country, scoring 37 goals.
footballers.story: The non-flying Dutchman, who would not board a plane and still became the most elegant footballer in England. Bergkamp's time at Inter was miserable and his time at Arsenal was transformative: he was the first foreign star to say yes to the club, and he arrived at a place that then won three titles and a Cup Winners' Cup, and went a whole league season unbeaten with him in the side. He once took all three places in Match of the Day's goal of the month, which no one else has done. There is a statue of him outside the Emirates and a place in the Premier League Hall of Fame. The touch, people still say, was the best there has been.
didYouKnow: His father named him after Denis Law, with an extra letter added because the registrar rejected the original spelling.
His fear of flying earned him the nickname the Non-Flying Dutchman.
His goal against Newcastle in 2002 was voted the best goal of the Premier League's first twenty five years.

footballers.name: Frederic Kanoute
clues: I won two UEFA Cups back to back and never won a league title anywhere.
I was born in France, played for France's under twenty ones, and ended up playing for Mali.
I scored on my Tottenham debut, nine minutes after coming on for Bobby Zamora.
I played for West Ham and Tottenham before I became a star in Spain.
I am the six foot four striker who is still Sevilla's highest scoring foreigner.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 2nd of September 1977. I played 38 times for my country, scoring 23 goals.
footballers.story: African Footballer of the Year, and the first winner born in Europe. Kanoute was French, chose Mali, and became the best thing to happen to Sevilla in a generation, winning two UEFA Cups and scoring against everybody. Before that he had been a West Ham and Tottenham striker who looked too languid to be as good as he was. He is remembered as much for his convictions: he covered up a betting company's logo on his shirt because his faith forbade it, and he paid for a mosque in Seville out of his own pocket when it was about to close. Thirty nine caps, and a presence larger than the statistics.
didYouKnow: Born in France, he was the first player born outside Africa to be named African Footballer of the Year.
He put more than seven hundred thousand dollars of his own money into buying a mosque in Seville.
He refused to wear Sevilla's gambling sponsor on religious grounds, so the club made him a brand free shirt.

footballers.name: Seamus Coleman
clues: I gave one club seventeen years and climbed into their all-time top ten for appearances.
I was in the PFA 2013-14 team of the year under Roberto Martinez.
I passed Dixie Dean on my club's all-time appearance list.
I managed Everton for one match, alongside Leighton Baines.
I played right back for the Republic of Ireland at one European Championship.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 11th of October 1988. I played 81 times for my country, scoring 1 goal.
footballers.story: Sixty thousand pounds, seventeen years, one club. Everton plucked Coleman out of Sligo Rovers on a scout's recommendation and got the bargain of a generation, a Gaelic footballer turned overlapping right-back who simply never stopped turning up. He made the PFA Team of the Year under Roberto Martinez, climbed past Dixie Dean into Everton's all-time top ten for appearances, and captained the side in the final game ever played at Goodison Park. A Neil Taylor tackle broke his leg in two places in 2017 and FIFA paid his wages while he rebuilt it. He even managed the club for a night, alongside Leighton Baines. Eighty one caps for Ireland, and not one of them handed to him.
footballers.numbers: 1 goal in 81 caps for Republic of Ireland
didYouKnow: Everton signed him from Sligo Rovers for sixty thousand pounds in January 2009.
He fractured both his tibia and fibula in a 2017 World Cup qualifier after a tackle by Neil Taylor.
He was Everton's joint interim manager alongside Leighton Baines in January 2025, winning an FA Cup tie against Peterborough.

footballers.name: Shaun Wright-Phillips
clues: I cost twenty one million pounds and scored four league goals in three years.
I have played for both Chelsea and Manchester City.
I won young player of the year four seasons running at one club.
My brother is the New York Red Bulls' all-time leading scorer.
My dad adopted me when I was three, and he is the one everybody has heard of.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 25th of October 1981. I played 36 times for my country, scoring 6 goals.
footballers.story: Released as a teenager, and an England international by twenty two. Wright-Phillips came through Manchester City's youth system after Nottingham Forest let him go, scored on his England debut, and was good enough that Chelsea paid a large fee for him, where he mostly sat on the bench and won a title anyway. Back at City he was better. Queens Park Rangers and New York followed, where he played alongside his own famous relative's legacy in a different league. Thirty six caps. His adoptive father is one of the most celebrated strikers in Arsenal's history, and his brother played for England too.
didYouKnow: He is the adopted son of the England striker Ian Wright, who adopted him when he was three.
He scored on his England debut, the third goal in a 3-0 win over Ukraine in 2004.
His younger brother Bradley is the all time leading scorer for the New York Red Bulls.

footballers.name: John McGinn
clues: I was speared in the thigh by a training pole thrown by my own club captain, and I took the club to court.
I joke that nobody in football has a backside as big as mine.
I scored my country's only goal at a World Cup, and it was our first win there in thirty six years.
I captained my club to a European trophy, only the third man ever to do it there.
I currently play for Aston Villa.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 18th of October 1994. I played 92 times for my country, scoring 22 goals.
footballers.story: Scotland's midfield for a decade, and Aston Villa's engine for longer than anyone expected. McGinn came from Hibernian, where he had won a Scottish Cup that ended a hundred and fourteen year wait, for a fee that now looks absurd. At Villa he scored in a play-off final to get them promoted, then stayed to captain them back into the Champions League. Steven Gerrard said he was the best player he had seen in training since he stopped playing with the very best. More than ninety Scotland caps and over twenty goals, and a brother who also played professionally. Everything he does looks slightly too energetic.
didYouKnow: He scored in Aston Villa's 2019 Championship play-off final win over Derby at Wembley.
He captained Aston Villa to the Europa League title in 2026, only the third man to lead the club to a European trophy.
His older brothers Paul and Stephen were also professional footballers, and all three played for St Mirren and Hibernian.

footballers.name: Shola Ameobi
clues: I played twenty times for England at under twenty one level and then chose Nigeria.
I scored at the Nou Camp against Barcelona.
I scored seven times against Sunderland, and only Jackie Milburn has done better for my club.
On my club's all-competitions European scoring list, only Alan Shearer is ahead of me.
I was Newcastle's first loan manager, and I still work for the club off the pitch.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 12th of October 1981. I played 10 times for my country, scoring 2 goals.
footballers.story: Fourteen years at one club, which for a striker who scored at his rate is almost inexplicable, and entirely admirable. Ameobi got seventy nine goals for Newcastle across nearly four hundred games and was simultaneously a cult hero and a running joke, which is the hardest balance in football to hold. He scored in the four four against Arsenal. He was born in Nigeria, raised in Newcastle, and played ten times for Nigeria late on. The exchange about what Jose Mourinho calls him, to which the answer was simply his own first name, is one of the great deadpan moments of the Premier League era.
didYouKnow: He was born in Zaria, Nigeria, and moved to Newcastle upon Tyne when he was five.
His scoring record against Sunderland led Newcastle supporters to nickname him the Mackem Slayer.
He played twenty times for England at under twenty one level before switching to Nigeria.

footballers.name: Guti
clues: I joined my club's academy at ten years old and left twenty four years later.
I won five league titles in Spain.
My no-look backheel set up Karim Benzema at Deportivo.
The blond hair and the temper were as famous as the passing.
I played in the Galactico era at Real Madrid.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 31st of October 1976. I played 13 times for my country, scoring 3 goals.
footballers.story: Real Madrid for seventeen years, and the most beautiful pass of the century. Guti came through the academy as a striker, became a midfielder, and spent his career as the Galactico who was not quite a Galactico, in and out of the side while collecting five league titles and three European Cups. The pass everyone remembers is a no-look backheel through a defence to set up Karim Benzema, which looks impossible every time you watch it. Spain gave him only thirteen caps, partly because of the temperament, partly because of the era. He finished at Besiktas and has coached since. Maddening, lazy, and occasionally the best footballer alive.
didYouKnow: He joined Real Madrid's academy at ten years old and left twenty four years later.
He began as a striker before his manager converted him into a playmaker.
He won three European Cups and never played a minute at a World Cup or a European Championship.

footballers.name: Chris Smalling
clues: My manager publicly called me stupid for getting sent off in a derby.
I won the first ever Europa Conference League and was man of the match in the final.
I won two Premier League titles and later played in Saudi Arabia and Portugal.
I am a centre back who played under Jose Mourinho at two different clubs.
I came through at Millwall and grew up supporting Arsenal.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 22nd of November 1989. I played 31 times for my country, scoring 1 goal.
footballers.story: Non-league to Old Trafford in two years. Smalling was playing for Maidstone United while studying at university when Fulham spotted him, and barely a season later Manchester United paid seven million pounds for a defender with twelve top-flight appearances. Two Premier League titles followed, and so did the criticism, including a manager telling the press in public that he and his partner were not brave enough. Rome fixed all that. He went to Roma on loan, stayed five years, won a European trophy under Jose Mourinho and was adored in a way he never quite was in England. Thirty one caps. Vegan, and happy to talk about it.
didYouKnow: He was a schoolboy national judo champion and came second in an international competition.
He was the first player in Premier League history to score two first half goals as a substitute.
He was man of the match in the 2022 Europa Conference League final, which Roma won as the inaugural winners.

footballers.name: Oliver Kahn
clues: I played for two clubs in my life and both were German.
I was voted Europe's best goalkeeper four years running.
I won the Champions League in 2000-01.
But I famously lost a Champions League final to a late comeback.
They called me the Titan, and I was in goal when England won five one in Munich.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 15th of June 1969. I played 86 times for my country, scoring 0 goals.
footballers.story: The only goalkeeper ever to win the Golden Ball at a World Cup, and he spent the final itself making the mistake everyone remembers. Kahn was Der Titan, the most intimidating presence in the Bundesliga for a decade and a half, and he won eight league titles and a Champions League with Bayern Munich, saving three penalties in the shootout in the final. Before Bayern there was Karlsruher SC. Eighty six caps, and a rivalry with Jens Lehmann that defined German goalkeeping for years. He came back as the club's chief executive, where he discovered that the job is harder from a desk.
didYouKnow: He is the only goalkeeper ever to win the Golden Ball as the best player at a World Cup, taking it in 2002.
He saved three penalties in the shootout to win Bayern Munich the 2001 Champions League final against Valencia.
He was sent off in 2001 after going up for a corner and punching the ball into the net.

footballers.name: Christian Vieri
clues: I won the trophy for the worst player in Serie A, and I had once been the most expensive footballer in the world.
I played for Juventus, Inter and AC Milan.
I won a Golden Boot in Spain and a Golden Boot in Italy, and only ever one league title.
I grew up in Sydney and I was better at cricket than football as a boy.
They called me Bobo, and I started a fashion label with Paolo Maldini.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 12th of July 1973. I played 49 times for my country, scoring 23 goals.
footballers.story: A club collector with a goal in him. Bobo Vieri played for both Milan clubs, both Turin clubs, Lazio, Atletico Madrid, Monaco and Fiorentina, among others, and never settled anywhere because somebody always paid more. Lazio sold him to Inter for a world record fee. He was the top scorer at the 1998 World Cup, got twenty three goals in forty nine games for Italy, and won precisely one Serie A title in all of it. Italy also voted him the biggest waste of talent in the league one year, which tells you how high the expectations were. Nine goals in nine World Cup matches. Nobody ever doubted the ability.
didYouKnow: He grew up in Sydney after his footballer father moved to Australia, and played youth football there.
Inter Milan signed him from Lazio in 1999 for what was then a world record fee.
He won the Golden Boot in Spain with Atletico Madrid and the Capocannoniere in Italy with Inter.

footballers.name: Marcelo
clues: I won a Copa Libertadores back home after fifteen years in Spain.
I scored the opening goal of a World Cup in my own country, and it was an own goal.
Roberto Carlos says I am the best left back in Real Madrid's history.
I won five European Cups.
I was a left back who frankly could not defend.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 12th of May 1988. I played 58 times for my country, scoring 6 goals.
footballers.story: Twenty five trophies, more than any player in Real Madrid's history. Marcelo arrived at eighteen from Fluminense and stayed fifteen years, redefining what a left-back could be and winning five Champions Leagues, the last of them as club captain. He was never a defender in the conventional sense and it did not matter, because almost nobody got past him and because the attacking was worth any risk. Fifty eight caps for Brazil, two Olympic bronzes, and the misfortune of a generation that never won a World Cup. He went home to Fluminense at the end and won the Copa Libertadores there too.
didYouKnow: He overtook Paco Gento to become the most decorated player in Real Madrid's history.
He was the first foreign player to captain Real Madrid in more than a century.
He scored the opening goal of the 2014 World Cup in his own country, and it was an own goal.

footballers.name: Ivan Toney
clues: I scored thirty one goals in a single Championship season, which nobody had managed before.
I turned down the chance to play for Jamaica.
I came on in extra time at a Euros for one reason, and I scored the penalty.
I left the Premier League for Saudi Arabia for a reported forty million pounds.
I scored sixty seven league goals for Brentford.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 16th of March 1996. I played 10 times for my country, scoring 1 goal.
footballers.story: A penalty taker so reliable that people stopped watching the goalkeeper. Toney came up through Newcastle's youth system without ever really playing, scored thirty one in a Championship season for Brentford, and then became the Premier League striker nobody could keep quiet. Then came an eight month ban for hundreds of breaches of betting rules, some of them on his own matches. He came back and scored a penalty in his first game. Two England caps, a huge move to Saudi Arabia, and a career with a hole blown through the middle of it that he refilled almost immediately. Nerveless is the word.
didYouKnow: He scored thirty one goals in the 2020-21 Championship season, a record for the division.
He was banned from football for eight months in 2023 after 232 breaches of betting rules.
He was the youngest player ever to appear for Northampton Town, debuting at sixteen.

footballers.name: Juan Roman Riquelme
clues: I said people complain that I never smile, but I have never seen Zidane laugh either.
Louis van Gaal played me on the wing and mostly left me out.
I went back to Argentina for fifteen million dollars, the most an Argentine club had ever paid.
I was a Barcelona number ten who got loaned to a small Spanish club and was far better there.
Jens Lehmann saved a last minute penalty that would have taken a Champions League semi-final to extra time.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 24th of June 1978. I played 51 times for my country, scoring 17 goals.
footballers.story: The last of the true number tens, and he refused to be anything else. Riquelme would not run back, would not press, would not move out to the wing when Louis van Gaal asked him to at Barcelona, and so he barely played there. Everywhere he was allowed to stand still and receive the ball he was sublime: two Copa Libertadores and an Intercontinental Cup with Boca Juniors, and a Villarreal side he dragged to a Champions League semi-final before missing the penalty that would have taken them to the final. Olympic gold with Argentina, fifty one caps, and a reputation in Buenos Aires that borders on the religious.
didYouKnow: He was the eldest of eleven children in a poor family from San Fernando, Buenos Aires.
Louis van Gaal dismissed him at Barcelona as a political signing and he spent most of that contract on loan.
He has been president of Boca Juniors since 2023, the club where he was the defining player of its modern era.

footballers.name: Raul Meireles
clues: I was suspended for a Champions League final and still ended up a winner.
I played for Liverpool and then for Chelsea, one season each.
The same manager had me at Porto and at Chelsea.
I joked about winning the ink championship against Agger and Skrtel.
I went to two World Cups and two Euros for Portugal, but my last cap came two years before they won one.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 17th of March 1983. I played 76 times for my country, scoring 10 goals.
footballers.story: The mohawk, the tattoos, and a trophy collection that is quietly ridiculous. Meireles won a league title and a European trophy with Porto, moved to Liverpool and was voted their player of the year within a single season, then went to Chelsea and won a Champions League and a Europa League in two years. Add a Portuguese cup haul and a Turkish title at Fenerbahce and he has won more than most of the famous names of his era. Portugal capped him seventy six times and he reached a European Championship semi-final. He looked like a man in a band and ran like a man with a deadline.
didYouKnow: He won the Champions League with Chelsea in 2012 despite being suspended for the final.
He was voted the PFA Fans' Player of the Year during his single season at Liverpool.
He played at two World Cups and two European Championships for Portugal.

footballers.name: Gabriel Agbonlahor
clues: I scored a hat-trick with my head, my right foot and my left foot, all inside seven minutes.
I never moved for a transfer fee in my entire career.
I was given the captaincy after Stiliyan Petrov's leukaemia diagnosis, and I later resigned it after being photographed with a shisha pipe.
I turned down a Nigeria call-up, was named in a provisional Nigeria squad anyway, and I could have played for Scotland too.
I am the Birmingham born striker who gave Aston Villa his whole career and won nothing.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 13th of October 1986. I played 3 times for my country, scoring 0 goals.
footballers.story: One club, one city, and absolutely nothing to show for it. Agbonlahor came through Aston Villa's academy and stayed almost four hundred games, finishing as their all-time leading Premier League scorer, and in all that time he won not a single trophy. He lost a League Cup final and an FA Cup final instead. He was quick in a way that Premier League defences had no answer to in the late 2000s, got three England caps during the Capello years and then was never seen again. He captained the club, got relegated with it, and retired at thirty. Villa fans still argue about whether he was underrated or whether he stopped trying. Probably both.
didYouKnow: He spent his entire professional career at Aston Villa, the club he joined as a schoolboy in Birmingham.
He never moved for a transfer fee at any point in his career.
He was Aston Villa's record Premier League goalscorer until Ollie Watkins overtook him in May 2025.

footballers.name: Duncan Ferguson
clues: I became the most expensive footballer in Britain and played fourteen league games for the club that bought me.
I share the Premier League record for red cards with Patrick Vieira and Richard Dunne.
Burglars picked my house twice, and both times one of them ended up in hospital.
I have scored more Premier League goals than any other Scot.
I scored a hat-trick of headers, and nobody had done that in the Premier League before.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 27th of December 1971. I played 7 times for my country, scoring 0 goals.
footballers.story: A Scottish centre-forward who went to prison for something he did on a football pitch. Big Dunc headbutted an opponent while at Rangers and served three months, which is the most extreme item on a long list. He had two spells at Everton with a Newcastle detour in between, scored a famous amount with his head, and holds a share of the Premier League record for red cards. He fell out with Scotland and ended with only seven caps. Goodison adored him anyway, because he once chased two burglars out of his own house and because he always, always ran at people. He later managed the club he loved, twice, as caretaker.
didYouKnow: He served a prison sentence in 1995 over an on-field headbutt on the Raith Rovers defender John McStay.
He shares the record for the most red cards in Premier League history with eight.
He was the first player to score a Premier League hat-trick entirely with headers.

footballers.name: Luis Garcia
clues: I scored the winner against Juventus and the winner against Chelsea on the way to a European Cup final.
I was on Barcelona's books for four years without playing a first-team game, and they later had to buy me back.
Jose Mourinho called one of my goals a ghost goal.
The crowd sang that I drank sangria and came from Barca to bring them joy.
I won the Champions League with Liverpool in 2005 and never won a thing in Spain.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 24th of June 1978. I played 18 times for my country, scoring 4 goals.
footballers.story: He scored in every round of a Champions League they had no business winning. Garcia's goal against Chelsea in the semi-final may or may not have crossed the line, and twenty years later Liverpool and Chelsea supporters still cannot agree, which is exactly the point. He was at Anfield for three years, came from Barcelona, went to Atletico Madrid afterwards, and in that short window produced the most important goals of anyone in a red shirt. Twenty caps for Spain. The song the Kop wrote about him is still sung by people who never saw him play, which is a kind of immortality.
didYouKnow: His disputed ghost goal against Chelsea sent Liverpool through to the 2005 Champions League final.
He scored a hat-trick against Slovakia in a World Cup qualifying play-off ahead of the 2006 tournament.
He was on Barcelona's books for four years without playing a first-team league game and they later bought him back.

footballers.name: Jack Wilshere
clues: I scored my first goal for my club ten days after my debut, at sixteen.
My manager said I had Spanish technique and an English heart.
I won the BBC goal of the season twice in a row, which nobody had done since the Premier League began.
My only major trophies are two FA Cups, and I never won a league title.
I was my club's youngest ever league debutant, and I took the record off Cesc Fabregas.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 1st of January 1992. I played 34 times for my country, scoring 2 goals.
footballers.story: Arsenal versus Barcelona, 2011, and for ninety minutes he was the best midfielder on the pitch. Wilshere was nineteen. The problem was never the talent, it was the ankles and the shins, and he spent the next decade having the career taken away from him a few months at a time. He still managed two FA Cups, thirty four England caps and a goal against Slovenia that lifted a whole stadium, plus the team goal against Norwich he started and finished. West Ham and Bournemouth followed, then retirement at thirty. He coaches Arsenal's youngsters now, which is where he started.
didYouKnow: He became Arsenal's youngest ever league debutant at 16 years and 256 days, breaking Cesc Fabregas' record.
He won the BBC Goal of the Season award in two consecutive seasons, 2013-14 and 2014-15.
He finished his playing career in Denmark with AGF Aarhus before retiring at thirty.

footballers.name: Nemanja Vidic
clues: I lost two Champions League finals and won one.
My transfer was agreed on Christmas Day and then I had to wait for a work permit.
I am the only defender to have been voted the Premier League's player of the season twice.
I won five league titles and three League Cups at one club, and never the FA Cup.
Robin van Persie said I put my head where other players were scared to put their feet.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 21st of October 1981. I played 56 times for my country, scoring 2 goals.
footballers.story: Half of the best central defensive partnership the Premier League has seen. Vidic came from Spartak Moscow in January, had a difficult first six months, and then spent eight years being the most uncompromising defender in England. Five league titles, a Champions League, and two Premier League Player of the Year awards, which almost no defender wins once. Serbia and Montenegro conceded one goal in their entire qualifying campaign for a World Cup with him in the side, and then he missed the tournament through injury and they were taken apart. Fifty six caps. Inter at the end. He simply did not go round people, and nobody went round him.
