honours: First League of Serbia and Montenegro (Red Star Belgrade, 2004)
didYouKnow: Manchester United agreed to sign him on Christmas Day 2005 and he arrived once his work permit came through.
He is the only defender ever to win the Premier League Player of the Season award twice.
Robin van Persie said he put his head where other players were scared to put their feet.

footballers.name: Patrick Kluivert
clues: I went out of three major tournaments in a row at the semi-final stage, and two of them went to penalties.
I held my country's goalscoring record until Robin van Persie passed me.
I spent six years at Barcelona and won one trophy.
I also played for Newcastle.
I was the six foot three Dutch striker who partnered Rivaldo at Barcelona.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 1st of July 1976. I played 79 times for my country, scoring 40 goals.
footballers.story: Eighteen years old, on as a substitute, and the winner in a European Cup final. Kluivert remains the youngest player ever to score in one, and that night with Ajax was the summit rather than the start of something. What followed was six years at Barcelona that produced exactly one trophy, a Dutch goalscoring record that stood until Robin van Persie passed it, and the cruellest pattern in international football: three major tournament semi-finals in a row, two of them lost on penalties. He also played for Newcastle, which fewer people remember. He has coached almost everywhere since, from Curacao to Barcelona's academy to Indonesia.
didYouKnow: He came off the bench at eighteen to score the winner in the 1995 Champions League final, and is still the youngest scorer in a final.
He scored a hat-trick in the 6-1 Euro 2000 quarter-final against Yugoslavia and shared the tournament's Golden Boot.
His forty goals were the Netherlands record until Robin van Persie passed him in 2013.

footballers.name: Theo Walcott
clues: I had a Nike contract at fourteen, before I had played a senior game.
My only medals are FA Cups, all of them with Arsenal.
Pep Guardiola reportedly said you would need a pistol to stop me.
I am still the youngest player ever to score a hat-trick for England, and it was my country's first competitive one in seven years.
I was picked for a World Cup squad at seventeen without ever having played a Premier League game, and I did not get on the pitch.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 16th of March 1989. I played 47 times for my country, scoring 8 goals.
footballers.story: Picked for a World Cup squad at seventeen without having played a single top-flight match. Walcott was Southampton's youngest ever player, cost Arsenal five million pounds as a schoolboy, and then spent twelve years at the club being both electrifying and slightly unsatisfying, which is the Arsenal condition. He scored a hat-trick for England in Croatia that remains one of the best away performances anyone has produced in that shirt, and still only got forty seven caps. Three FA Cups. Everton, then back to Southampton to finish where he started. The pace was real, and the chances it created never quite added up.
didYouKnow: He became England's youngest ever senior international at seventeen years and seventy five days.
He was picked for England's 2006 World Cup squad before he had played a single Premier League game.
He is still the youngest player ever to score a hat-trick for England.

footballers.name: Jussi Jaaskelainen
clues: I won fifty six caps and never played at a single tournament, because we never qualified.
I was bought for a hundred thousand pounds and played five hundred and thirty games for the club.
A double save of mine was voted third best in the Premier League's first twenty years.
I played most famously under Big Sam.
I bet you cannot spell my name.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 19th of April 1975. I played 56 times for my country, scoring 0 goals.
footballers.story: Bolton Wanderers for fifteen years, more than five hundred games, and a hundred thousand pounds well spent. Jaaskelainen came from Vaasa in Finland for the kind of fee that would not buy a Premier League substitute now, and ended up as one of the best shot-stoppers in the division across an era when Bolton were in Europe and beating everybody. He saved two penalties in the same match against Blackburn, which is the clip Bolton fans still share. Then West Ham and Wigan. Fifty six caps for a Finland side that never qualified for anything, which is the only medal missing from a career of remarkable consistency.
didYouKnow: Bolton bought him from VPS for a hundred thousand pounds in 1997, after a trial at Norwich City.
He made 530 appearances for Bolton across fifteen seasons.
He won fifty six caps for Finland and never played at a major tournament, because they never qualified.

footballers.name: Gonzalo Higuain
clues: I was born in France, I do not speak French, and I had to apply for the nationality of the country I played for.
The same manager had me at Napoli, Juventus and Chelsea.
I was only the third Argentine to score a World Cup hat-trick, after Batistuta and one man in 1930.
My only English trophy was a Europa League, won on loan.
I won three La Liga titles and three Serie A titles and never a single trophy with my country.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 10th of December 1987. I played 75 times for my country, scoring 31 goals.
footballers.story: Three finals in three summers, and a nation that never forgave him. Higuain was a genuinely outstanding striker, the man who scored thirty six goals in a single Serie A season for Napoli to break a record that had stood since the 1920s, and the man Juventus then paid a vast fee to take off them. For Argentina he scored the quarter-final winner that took them to a World Cup final, and the missed chances in the finals that followed are what people remember. He was born in France because his father was playing there. Five La Liga titles and three Serie A titles, and a career defined by three afternoons.
didYouKnow: He was born in Brest because his father was playing in France, and he only took Argentine citizenship in 2007.
He scored thirty six goals for Napoli in 2015-16, still the record for a single Serie A season.
Juventus paid Napoli ninety million euros for him, then the largest fee an Italian club had ever paid.

footballers.name: Conor Coady
clues: I was the first player from my club to start for England since 1990.
I played centre-back, and I captained England's under-twenties at a World Cup.
England's assistant manager called me the player of the tournament at a Euros where I never got on the pitch.
I came through at Liverpool and played twice for them.
I now coach the England under twenty ones.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 25th of February 1993. I played 10 times for my country, scoring 1 goal.
footballers.story: The quietest two-tournament career England has produced. Coady went to a European Championship and a World Cup and did not play a minute of either, yet an England assistant called him the player of the tournament at the first one, for everything he did around the squad. He was the first Wolves player to start for England since Steve Bull in 1990, and he was so reliable that a run of eighty four consecutive Premier League games ended only because of a Covid contact. Two Championship titles, won at two different clubs. He was also named Football Ally of the Year at the British LGBT Awards. He coaches England's under twenty ones now.
didYouKnow: He played every minute of eighty four consecutive Premier League games for Wolves, a run of 7,560 minutes.
He was the first Wolves player to start for England since Steve Bull in 1990.
He was named Football Ally of the Year at the British LGBT Awards in 2021.

footballers.name: Robert Pires
clues: I was signed for six million pounds, replacing a winger who had left for Barcelona.
I scored eight times against Tottenham, and at their ground in five straight seasons.
I was taken off after eighteen minutes of a Champions League final because our goalkeeper was sent off, and it was my last game for the club.
I set up the golden goal that won a European Championship final.
I tried to pass a penalty to Thierry Henry, failed to make proper contact, and it went down as my miss.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 29th of October 1973. I played 79 times for my country, scoring 14 goals.
footballers.story: The best left foot in the Premier League for about four years, and a World Cup winner before he arrived. Pires came from Marseille with a France medal already in the bag and took a season to adjust, after which he was voted Footballer of the Year, won two league titles and three FA Cups, and was central to a side that went a whole season unbeaten. Seventy nine caps and a European Championship too. Villarreal got the late years and he turned up at Aston Villa at thirty six for a handful of games. He also took part in the most embarrassing penalty in Arsenal's history, which he has lived down.
didYouKnow: He came through the Metz academy and made his senior debut for them in 1993 against Lyon.
He scored against Tottenham on eight separate occasions during his Arsenal career.
He was made a Knight of the Legion of Honour in 1998 after France won the World Cup.

footballers.name: Thiago Motta
clues: I won two European Cups with two different clubs.
I have played international football for two countries that have both won World Cups.
I was sent off in a Champions League semi-final for a slap that Sergio Busquets may or may not have felt.
I won eighteen trophies at Paris Saint-Germain.
I am a football manager who recently managed Juventus.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 28th of August 1982. I played 30 times for my country, scoring 1 goal.
footballers.story: Brazilian by birth, Italian by international career, and now better known for a clipboard. Motta came through Barcelona's academy, won a Champions League there, then injuries pushed him to Atletico Madrid and Genoa before Inter made him a holding midfielder of real distinction and he won the treble. Paris Saint-Germain gave him five league titles. He played thirty times for Italy. Then he became a coach, invented a system he described with numbers that made no sense to anybody, took Bologna into the Champions League on a fraction of the money, and discovered at a much bigger club how quickly that goodwill evaporates.
didYouKnow: He played twice for Brazil in 2003 before switching to Italy in 2011 through his Italian ancestry.
He won the Champions League with two different clubs, Barcelona in 2006 and Inter in 2010.
He won eighteen trophies in his six years at Paris Saint-Germain.

footballers.name: Robbie Fowler
clues: I won young player of the year twice running and never once won the senior player of the year award.
I told the referee I had not been fouled, took the penalty anyway, missed it, and won a fair play award for it.
I once held the record for the fastest hat-trick in Premier League history, and it stood for twenty years.
My club fined me sixty thousand pounds for a celebration, and my manager told the press I had been eating grass.
I am in the top ten scorers in Premier League history and I never won a league title.
footballers.kickoff: I was born on the 9th of April 1975. I played 26 times for my country, scoring 7 goals.
footballers.story: They called him God on Merseyside, which tells you everything. Fowler scored a hundred and eighty three goals for Liverpool, including a hat-trick in four and a half minutes that stood as the fastest in Premier League history for over twenty years, and he was part of the treble side in 2001. England gave him only twenty six caps because Shearer, Sheringham and then Owen were in the way. Leeds, Manchester City and a brief emotional return to Anfield followed. He invested the money so well in property that his name became slang for being unexpectedly rich, which he has always found funny.
didYouKnow: He scored a hat-trick against Arsenal in 1994 in four minutes and thirty three seconds, a record that stood for twenty years.
Liverpool supporters nicknamed him God during his peak years at Anfield.
He told a referee he had not been fouled, took the penalty anyway, missed it, and won a fair play award for it.
